• Bacterial fermentation produces organic acids and gas.

category: Describe digestion and absorption of dietary carbohydrates along with inherited and acquired disorders (lactose intolerance, sucrase-isomaltase deficiency)
front: Explain the role of the Na+/K+ ATPase pump in the intestinal absorption of dietary carbohydrates.
back:
• Pumps 3 Na+ out and 2 K+ into the cell.
• Creates a low intracellular sodium concentration.
• Drives Na+-dependent glucose/galactose uptake via SGLT-1.
• Indirectly powers secondary active transport.

category: Describe digestion and absorption of dietary carbohydrates along with inherited and acquired disorders (lactose intolerance, sucrase-isomaltase deficiency)
front: Contrast the structural targets of salivary alpha-amylase with those of the intestinal isomaltase enzyme.
back:
• Alpha-amylase: Hydrolyzes internal alpha(1→4) glycosidic bonds in starch.
• Isomaltase: Hydrolyzes alpha(1→6) branch points in limit dextrins.
• Amylase produces dextrins; Isomaltase yields free glucose.

category: Describe digestion and absorption of dietary carbohydrates along with inherited and acquired disorders (lactose intolerance, sucrase-isomaltase deficiency)
front: Describe the mechanism of fructose uptake across the apical and basolateral membranes of the enterocyte.
back:
• Apical entry: Facilitated diffusion via GLUT-5.
• Basolateral exit: Facilitated diffusion via GLUT-2.
• Mechanism is entirely sodium-independent.
• Transport occurs down its concentration gradient.

category: Describe digestion and absorption of dietary carbohydrates along with inherited and acquired disorders (lactose intolerance, sucrase-isomaltase deficiency)
front: In the clinical evaluation of carbohydrate malabsorption, the diagnostic marker indicative of bacterial fermentation of undigested sugars in the colon is the [___].
back:
• Hydrogen Breath Test.
• Measures H2 gas produced by colonic flora.
• Gas is absorbed into blood and exhaled.
• High levels indicate lactose or sucrose intolerance.

category: Describe digestion and absorption of dietary carbohydrates along with inherited and acquired disorders (lactose intolerance, sucrase-isomaltase deficiency)
front: An adult patient presents with cramps and flatulence after milk consumption but tolerates yogurt. Explain the physiological basis for this dietary tolerance.
back:
• Acquired Lactase Deficiency (Lactose Intolerance).
• Yogurt contains live Lactobacillus cultures.
• Bacteria provide endogenous lactase enzyme.
• Self-digestion of lactose occurs within the intestine.

category: Describe digestion and absorption of dietary carbohydrates along with inherited and acquired disorders (lactose intolerance, sucrase-isomaltase deficiency)
front: A patient is diagnosed with a GLUT-2 deficiency (Fanconi-Bickel Syndrome). Compare the expected impact on glucose transport versus fructose transport in the small intestine.
back:
• Both glucose and fructose transport are impaired.
• GLUT-2 is the common exit for all monosaccharides.
• Causes accumulation of sugars within the enterocyte.
• Results in severe carbohydrate malabsorption and hepatomegaly.

category: Describe digestion and absorption of dietary carbohydrates along with inherited and acquired disorders (lactose intolerance, sucrase-isomaltase deficiency)
front: Distinguish the metabolic fate of dietary fiber (e.g., cellulose) from that of digestible polysaccharides in humans.
back:
• Digestible (Starch): Hydrolyzed by amylase to monosaccharides for absorption.
• Fiber (Cellulose): Contains beta(1→4) bonds; human enzymes cannot hydrolyze.
• Fate: Passes to colon for bacterial fermentation or excretion.
• Function: Increases bowel motility and bulk.

category: Describe digestion and absorption of dietary carbohydrates along with inherited and acquired disorders (lactose intolerance, sucrase-isomaltase deficiency)
front: Identify the specific anatomical site and cellular region where the final hydrolysis of disaccharides occurs.
back:
• Site: Duodenum and upper jejunum.
• Region: Brush border (microvilli) of enterocytes.
• Enzyme types: Membrane-bound disaccharidases (Lactase, Sucrase, Maltase).
• Products: Monosaccharides ready for immediate absorption.

category: Describe digestion and absorption of dietary carbohydrates along with inherited and acquired disorders (lactose intolerance, sucrase-isomaltase deficiency)
front: The primary enzyme responsible for initiating the digestion of starch in the oral cavity by hydrolyzing internal ̑̑̑(1→4) glycosidic bonds is [̑̑̑].
back: Salivary ̑-Amylase (Ptyalin). • Hydrolyzes random ̑(1→4) bonds in starch and glycogen. • Produces ̑-limit dextrins and maltose. • Inactivated by low gastric pH.

category: Describe digestion and absorption of dietary carbohydrates along with inherited and acquired disorders (lactose intolerance, sucrase-isomaltase deficiency)
front: A 25-year-old male experiences abdominal bloating, flatulence, and osmotic diarrhea shortly after consuming milk. An oral hydrogen breath test is positive. Identify the underlying biochemical defect.
back: Lactase Deficiency (Lactose Intolerance). • Inability to hydrolyze lactose into glucose and galactose. • Undigested lactose is fermented by colonic bacteria. • Produces H2, CO2, and organic acids.

category: Describe digestion and absorption of dietary carbohydrates along with inherited and acquired disorders (lactose intolerance, sucrase-isomaltase deficiency)
front: Explain how glucose and galactose are transported from the intestinal lumen into the enterocyte against their concentration gradient.
back: Secondary Active Transport (SGLT-1). • Co-transported with Na+ ions into the cell. • Driven by the Na+/K+ ATPase pump on the basolateral membrane. • Uses energy indirectly from the sodium electrochemical gradient.

category: Describe digestion and absorption of dietary carbohydrates along with inherited and acquired disorders (lactose intolerance, sucrase-isomaltase deficiency)
front: Contrast the substrate specificity and products of Sucrase and Isomaltase within the brush border enzyme complex.
back: • Sucrase: Hydrolyzes sucrose into glucose and fructose. • Isomaltase: Hydrolyzes ̑(1→6) bonds in isomaltose and ̑-limit dextrins. • Both are activities of a single bifunctional protein complex.

category: Describe digestion and absorption of dietary carbohydrates along with inherited and acquired disorders (lactose intolerance, sucrase-isomaltase deficiency)
front: Identify the sodium-independent transporter responsible for the facilitated diffusion of fructose across the apical membrane of the small intestine.
back: GLUT-5. • Specific for facilitated diffusion of fructose. • Does not require energy or sodium. • Located on the luminal (apical) surface of enterocytes.

category: Describe digestion and absorption of dietary carbohydrates along with inherited and acquired disorders (lactose intolerance, sucrase-isomaltase deficiency)
front: The common transporter located on the basolateral membrane that facilitates the exit of glucose, galactose, and fructose into the portal circulation is [̑̑̑].
back: GLUT-2. • Facilitated diffusion transporter for hexoses. • High capacity, low affinity system. • Moves sugars from enterocytes into the portal venous system.

category: Describe digestion and absorption of dietary carbohydrates along with inherited and acquired disorders (lactose intolerance, sucrase-isomaltase deficiency)
front: An infant presents with severe abdominal cramps and diarrhea after weaning onto a diet containing table sugar. Molecular testing reveals a genetic deficiency of the sucrase-isomaltase complex. Describe the pathophysiological consequence of this ingestion.
back: Sucrose Intolerance. • Undigested sucrose remains in the intestinal lumen. • Exerts osmotic pressure, drawing water into the gut (diarrhea). • Bacterial fermentation leads to gas and acidic stools.

category: Describe digestion and absorption of dietary carbohydrates along with inherited and acquired disorders (lactose intolerance, sucrase-isomaltase deficiency)
front: Describe the role of Pancreatic ̑-Amylase in the intestinal lumen and identify why it cannot achieve complete digestion of amylopectin.
back: • Hydrolyzes ̑(1→4) bonds randomly (endo-amylase). • Cannot hydrolyze ̑(1→6) branch points. • Digestion stops at ̑-limit dextrins, maltotriose, and maltose.

category: Describe digestion and absorption of dietary carbohydrates along with inherited and acquired disorders (lactose intolerance, sucrase-isomaltase deficiency)
front: Distinguish between the biochemical causes of Primary and Secondary Lactase Deficiency.
back: • Primary: Age-dependent genetic downregulation of lactase expression (common in adults). • Secondary: Acquired damage to intestinal mucosa (e.g., celiac disease, gastroenteritis). • Both result in lactose malabsorption and osmotic symptoms.

category: Describe digestion and absorption of dietary carbohydrates along with inherited and acquired disorders (lactose intolerance, sucrase-isomaltase deficiency)
front: Name the specific end-products of dietary carbohydrate digestion that are ultimately absorbed by the small intestine into the portal venous system.
back: Monosaccharides (Glucose, Galactose, Fructose). • Only single sugar units are absorbable. • Polysaccharides must be hydrolyzed to these units. • Transported to the liver for systemic distribution.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: The glucose transporter that is uniquely sequestered in intracellular vesicles and translocates to the plasma membrane only in response to insulin is [___].
back:
• GLUT-4
• Primarily found in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue.
• Mediates insulin-dependent glucose uptake.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: A neonate presents with jaundice, vomiting, and hepatomegaly shortly after starting breast milk. Laboratory tests show negative glucose in urine but positive reducing sugars. This indicates a deficiency in the enzyme responsible for creating [___] from Galactose 1-P.
back:
• UDP-Glucose (via GALT enzyme).
• Deficiency causes Classic Galactosemia.
• Leads to Galactose 1-P and galactitol accumulation.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Explain the energy-coupling mechanism used by the SGLT-1 transporter for glucose absorption in the intestinal mucosa.
back:
• Secondary active transport.
• Couples glucose uptake with the Na+ concentration gradient.
• Gradient is maintained by the Na+/K+ ATPase pump.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Contrast GLUT-1 and GLUT-2 regarding their tissue distribution and functional response to blood glucose fluctuations.
back:
• GLUT-1: High-affinity (low Km); found in RBCs/Blood-Brain Barrier for basal uptake.
• GLUT-2: Low-affinity (high Km); bidirectional transport in liver/pancreas responding to high glucose.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Identify the specific monosaccharide transporter in the small intestine and testes that shows high specificity for fructose rather than glucose.
back:
• GLUT-5.
• Primary sodium-independent fructose transporter.
• Utilizes facilitated diffusion.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: In the pancreatic beta cells and liver, [___] acts as a 'glucose sensor' due to its high Km and high Vmax compared to hexokinase.
back:
• Glucokinase (Hexokinase IV).
• Functions only during hyperglycemia.
• Not inhibited by Glucose 6-phosphate.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: A chronic diabetic patient presents with cataracts. This pathology results from the osmotic effects of [___] produced by aldose reductase when glucose levels are high.
back:
• Sorbitol (Glucitol).
• Trapped inside cells (lens, retina, nerves).
• Causes water retention and cellular swelling.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Explain the molecular event occurring at the GLUT-4 vesicle when insulin binds to the tyrosine kinase receptor in myocytes.
back:
• Signaling cascade triggers vesicle translocation.
• Vesicles fuse with the plasma membrane.
• Increases the density of transporters for rapid uptake.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Distinguish between the Na+-independent (GLUT) and Na+-dependent (SGLT) transport systems regarding their driving forces.
back:
• GLUT: Facilitated diffusion; moves glucose down its concentration gradient.
• SGLT: Secondary active transport; moves glucose against its gradient using Na+ energy.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Name the primary glucose transporter isoform responsible for glucose uptake in neurons to ensure a consistent CNS energy supply.
back:
• GLUT-3.
• High-affinity transporter.
• Maintains glucose entry even during low blood concentrations.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: The glucose transporter specifically located in the skeletal muscle and adipose tissue that remains sequestered in intracellular vesicles until stimulated by insulin is [___].
back: GLUT-4. • Translocates to the plasma membrane in response to insulin. • Primary mediator of postprandial glucose uptake in peripheral tissues.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: A newborn presents with severe osmotic diarrhea shortly after starting breast milk. Lab tests show malabsorption of glucose and galactose, but fructose is absorbed normally. Identify the underlying defective transporter.
back: SGLT-1. • Responsible for Na+-dependent secondary active transport of glucose and galactose. • Located in the brush border of intestinal mucosal cells.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Explain the bidirectional capability of the GLUT-2 transporter found in hepatocytes.
back: • High-capacity, low-affinity (high Km) system. • Transports glucose into the liver during the fed state (hyperglycemia). • Transports glucose out of the liver during fasting (glycogenolysis/gluconeogenesis).

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Contrast the energy requirements and driving forces between the SGLT and GLUT transport systems.
back: SGLT: • Secondary active transport. • Requires ATP indirectly (via Na+/K+ ATPase). • Driven by Na+ gradient. GLUT: • Facilitated diffusion. • Passive (no ATP). • Driven by glucose concentration gradient.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: List the primary physiological role and kinetic significance of the GLUT-3 transporter in the central nervous system.
back: • Primary glucose transporter in neurons. • Low Km (high affinity) ensures constant glucose uptake even during hypoglycemia. • Maintains energy supply to brain tissue.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: The specialized transporter used for the facilitative absorption of dietary fructose in the small intestine and found in spermatozoa is [___].
back: GLUT-5. • Specific for fructose transport, not glucose. • Found in the jejunum and testes.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: A patient with uncontrolled diabetes mellitus has persistent hyperglycemia. Despite this, their brain cells and erythrocytes continue to uptake glucose at a nearly constant rate. Which transporter kinetic feature allows this?
back: Low Km (High Affinity) of GLUT-1 and GLUT-3. • These transporters are saturated at normal glucose levels. • Ensures a baseline glucose supply regardless of high systemic fluctuations.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Describe the molecular mechanism of GLUT-4 translocation following insulin receptor activation.
back: • Insulin binds to Tyrosine Kinase receptor. • Activates PI3-kinase pathway. • Triggers fusion of GLUT-4 storage vesicles with the plasma membrane. • Increases glucose uptake capacity 10-20 fold.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Distinguish between the primary functions of SGLT-1 and SGLT-2 in the body.
back: SGLT-1: • Intestinal absorption of glucose and galactose. • Found in small intestine. SGLT-2: • Renal reabsorption of filtered glucose. • Found in Proximal Convoluted Tubules (PCT).

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Which glucose transporter serves as the 'glucose sensor' in pancreatic beta cells to regulate insulin secretion?
back: GLUT-2. • High Km ensures that glucose entry is proportional to blood glucose levels. • Links systemic hyperglycemia directly to insulin release.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: The insulin-dependent glucose transporter found primarily in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue, which translocates to the cell membrane in response to systemic signaling, is [___].
back:
• GLUT-4
• High affinity for glucose
• Regulated by insulin-mediated signaling cascades
• Key target in Type 2 Diabetes mellitus pathophysiology.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
coreConcept: Oral Rehydration Therapy Mechanism via SGLT-1
front: A 10-year-old child with severe watery diarrhea is treated with an oral solution containing glucose and sodium. The mechanism facilitating this therapeutic intestinal absorption is [___].
back:
• SGLT-1 (Secondary Active Transport)
• Couples Na+ movement down its gradient with glucose uptake
• Utilizes energy from the basolateral Na+/K+ ATPase pump
• Found in small intestinal mucosa and renal tubules.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Explain the role of GLUT-2 as a 'glucose sensor' in pancreatic beta-cells during hyperglycemia.
back:
• High Km (low affinity) ensures glucose entry is proportional to blood concentration
• High Vmax facilitates rapid uptake during post-prandial peaks
• Initiates ATP production, leading to insulin secretion cascade.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Contrast the glucose transport systems of the Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB) with those found in renal proximal tubules regarding energy requirement and mechanism.
back:
• BBB: GLUT-1 (Facilitated diffusion); insulin-independent; uses concentration gradients
• Renal Tubules: SGLT-2/SGLT-1 (Secondary active transport); requires energy via Na+ gradients; concentrates glucose against gradients.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Identify the specific transporter isoform responsible for dietary fructose absorption across the luminal membrane of the small intestine.
back:
• GLUT-5
• Sodium-independent transporter
• Specific for fructose, not glucose
• Found in intestine, testes, and kidneys.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: In the post-absorptive state, the liver utilizes the [___] transporter to allow glucose to exit hepatocytes and maintain normoglycemia.
back:
• GLUT-2
• Bi-directional transport capability
• Facilitates both glucose uptake and release depending on blood levels
• Insulin-independent mechanism.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
coreConcept: CNS Glucose Priority and Transporter Affinity
front: A patient presents with high blood glucose but normal brain function. Apply the concept of transporter affinity to explain why the central nervous system remains unaffected by peripheral insulin resistance.
back:
• Brain uses GLUT-3 (neurons) and GLUT-1 (BBB)
• Both have very low Km (high affinity)
• Ensure constant glucose supply even at low levels
• Transport is insulin-independent.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: How does the Na+/K+ ATPase pump indirectly facilitate glucose reabsorption in the SGLT-2 system of the nephron?
back:
• Pumps 3 Na+ out and 2 K+ in at the basolateral membrane
• Creates a low intracellular Na+ concentration
• This drives Na+ and glucose entry across the apical membrane via SGLT.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Compare GLUT-1 and GLUT-2 in terms of their physiological Km values and their typical anatomic locations.
back:
• GLUT-1: Low Km (high affinity); found in RBCs and BBB for constant uptake
• GLUT-2: High Km (low affinity); found in Liver and Pancreas for sensing glucose levels.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Name the primary glucose transporter located in the plasma membrane of mature erythrocytes.
back:
• GLUT-1
• Facilitated diffusion
• Insulin-independent
• Essential for RBCs as they lack mitochondria and rely on glycolysis.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: The transport of glucose into adipose tissue and skeletal muscle is primarily mediated by [___], which is the only insulin-dependent glucose transporter isoform.
back:
• GLUT-4
• Translocates from intracellular vesicles to the cell membrane in response to insulin.
• Found in muscle and adipose tissue.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: A 45-year-old diabetic patient has chronic hyperglycemia. Despite insulin deficiency, glucose continues to enter his hepatocytes and pancreatic beta-cells freely. This is due to the presence of [___].
back:
• GLUT-2
• It is an insulin-independent transporter.
• Has a high Km (low affinity), allowing it to act as a glucose sensor in the liver and pancreas.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Explain the mechanism of glucose absorption across the apical membrane of intestinal epithelial cells.
back:
• Secondary Active Transport (SGLT-1):
• Uses energy from the Na+ gradient created by the Na+/K+ ATPase pump.
• Glucose is cotransported with Na+ against its concentration gradient.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Contrast the transport mechanisms of glucose and fructose across the luminal (apical) membrane of the small intestine.
back:
• Glucose: Absorbed via SGLT-1 (Secondary Active Transport; Na+-dependent).
• Fructose: Absorbed via GLUT-5 (Facilitated Diffusion; Na+-independent).

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Describe the specialized role of the GLUT-1 transporter in the central nervous system and blood.
back:
• GLUT-1:
• Abundant in erythrocytes and the Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB).
• Provides continuous, insulin-independent basal glucose uptake for the brain.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: In the kidneys, the secondary active transport system responsible for reabsorbing filtered glucose from the proximal tubule is known as the [___] system.
back:
• SGLT (Sodium-dependent Glucose Transporter)
• Couples glucose reabsorption with Na+ influx.
• Essential for preventing glucosuria in healthy individuals.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: A laboratory study identifies a transporter with a very low Km (high affinity) for glucose, ensuring constant uptake even during hypoglycemia. This transporter, found primarily in neurons, is [___].
back:
• GLUT-3
• Primary glucose transporter in neurons.
• Low Km ensures brain glucose supply is prioritized even at low blood concentrations.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: How does the translocation of GLUT-4 occur in response to insulin signaling?
back:
• Insulin binding to receptors triggers an intracellular signaling cascade.
• This causes GLUT-4-containing vesicles to fuse with the plasma membrane.
• Increases the Vmax of glucose uptake in muscle/fat.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Distinguish between the energetic requirements of GLUT and SGLT transport systems.
back:
• GLUT: Facilitated diffusion (Passive); follows concentration gradient; no energy used.
• SGLT: Secondary Active Transport; requires energy indirectly via Na+/K+ ATPase pump.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Identify the transporter responsible for the efflux of glucose, fructose, and galactose from the basolateral membrane of enterocytes into the portal circulation.
back:
• GLUT-2
• Located on the basolateral membrane of intestinal mucosal cells.
• Facilitates exit of all three monosaccharides into the blood via facilitated diffusion.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: The glucose transporter isoform primarily responsible for uptake into neurons is [___].
back:
• GLUT-3
• High-affinity glucose transporter
• Ensures consistent glucose delivery to the central nervous system

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: A patient presents with hyperglycemia. Insulin administration increases glucose uptake specifically in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue by translocation of [___].
back:
• GLUT-4
• Translocates from intracellular vesicles to the cell membrane
• Primary insulin-dependent glucose transporter

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Explain the secondary active transport mechanism used by SGLT-1 in the intestinal mucosa.
back:
• Couples glucose uptake with a Na+ gradient
• Uses Na+/K+ ATPase to maintain the electrochemical gradient
• Transports glucose against its concentration gradient

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Contrast the kinetic properties and functional roles of GLUT-2 in hepatocytes versus GLUT-4 in myocytes.
back:
• GLUT-2: High Km (low affinity), bidirectional, insulin-independent, acts as a glucose sensor
• GLUT-4: Low Km (high affinity), unidirectional uptake, insulin-dependent, regulates postprandial disposal

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Identify the specific transporter and mechanism responsible for fructose absorption in the small intestine.
back:
• GLUT-5
• Mechanism: Facilitated diffusion
• Sodium-independent monosaccharide transporter

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: The process by which GLUT proteins transport glucose across cell membranes down a concentration gradient is known as [___].
back:
• Facilitated diffusion
• Uses carrier proteins (GLUT isoforms)
• Energy-independent (passive) process

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: A neonate with osmotic diarrhea is suspected of having a defect in the transport of glucose and galactose across the brush border. Name the primary transporter involved.
back:
• SGLT-1 (Sodium-dependent glucose transporter 1)
• Transports both glucose and galactose via secondary active transport
• Located in the intestinal mucosa

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Explain how the high Km property of GLUT-2 facilitates the 'glucose sensor' role in pancreatic beta cells.
back:
• Allows glucose entry proportional to blood glucose levels
• Rapid equilibration ensures intracellular glucose matches plasma levels
• Triggers insulin release via ATP production and K+ channel closure

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Distinguish between the energy requirements of the GLUT-mediated and SGLT-mediated transport systems.
back:
• GLUT: Passive facilitated diffusion; requires no energy
• SGLT: Secondary active transport; indirectly requires ATP for the Na+/K+ pump

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: List the two primary anatomic locations where the SGLT-1 transporter is functionally essential for glucose absorption or recovery.
back:
• Small intestine (intestinal mucosa)
• Kidney (renal tubules)
• Essential for dietary absorption and preventing glucosuria

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: The insulin-dependent glucose transporter found primarily in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue is [___].
back:
• GLUT4
• Translocates from intracellular vesicles to the plasma membrane in response to insulin or exercise.
• Crucial for post-prandial glucose lowering.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: A 55-year-old diabetic is started on a gliflozin drug. This agent lowers blood glucose by inhibiting glucose reabsorption in the [___] of the nephron.
back:
• Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT)
• Target: SGLT2 (Sodium-Glucose Co-transporter 2).
• Mechanism: Inhibits secondary active transport, leading to therapeutic glucosuria.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Explain the secondary active transport mechanism utilized by SGLT1 for glucose absorption in the small intestine.
back:
• Energy Source: Derived from the Na+ gradient created by the basolateral Na+/K+ ATPase.
• Mechanism: Na+ flows down its electrochemical gradient, pulling glucose into the enterocyte against its concentration gradient.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: A neonate presents with microcephaly and refractory seizures. CSF analysis reveals low glucose despite normal serum levels. A deficiency in which specific transporter is suspected?
back:
• GLUT1 (De Vivo Syndrome)
• Function: Essential for glucose transport across the Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB) and into RBCs.
• Clinical hallmark: Low CSF-to-blood glucose ratio.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Outline the intracellular signaling steps that lead to GLUT4 recruitment in myocytes.
back:
• Insulin binds Tyrosine Kinase Receptor.
• Activation of Insulin Receptor Substrate (IRS-1) and PI3K/Akt pathway.
• Stimulates exocytosis of GLUT4-containing vesicles to the plasma membrane.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: The primary transporter responsible for the facilitated diffusion of dietary fructose across the luminal membrane of the enterocyte is [___].
back:
• GLUT5
• Specificity: High affinity for fructose; does not transport glucose or galactose.
• Mechanism: Facilitated diffusion (energy-independent).

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: A patient is diagnosed with Fanconi-Bickel Syndrome, characterized by glycogen accumulation and glucose intolerance. Which transporter is mutated in this condition?
back:
• GLUT2
• Localization: Liver, Pancreatic β-cells, kidney, and small intestine.
• Impact: Bidirectional glucose flux is impaired, leading to hepatorenal glycogen storage.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: How does the high Km (low affinity) of GLUT2 in pancreatic β-cells serve a metabolic monitoring function?
back:
• Glucose Sensor: Glucose entry is directly proportional to blood levels.
• Result: Increased glucose metabolism leads to high ATP, triggering insulin release only when hyperglycemia is present.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Contrast the glucose transport kinetics of GLUT1 versus GLUT2.
back:
• GLUT1: Low Km (High Affinity); provides constant, basal glucose uptake (e.g., Brain, RBCs).
• GLUT2: High Km (Low Affinity); active during hyperglycemia (e.g., Liver post-prandially).

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Identify the specific transporters located at the apical vs. basolateral membranes of a small intestinal enterocyte during glucose absorption.
back:
• Apical (Lumen): SGLT1 (Secondary active transport with Na+).
• Basolateral (Blood): GLUT2 (Facilitated diffusion).
• This arrangement ensures unidirectional glucose movement into the portal blood.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: The primary glucose transporter isoform that facilitates glucose entry across the blood-brain barrier and into erythrocytes is [___].
back:
* GLUT-1
* High affinity for glucose
* Ensures constant glucose supply
* Insulin-independent

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: A 45-year-old male with untreated Type 1 Diabetes presents with high blood glucose. His adipocytes cannot effectively take up glucose because [___] transporters remain sequestered in intracellular vesicles.
back:
* GLUT-4
* Requires insulin for translocation to cell membrane
* Found in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue
* Major site of post-prandial glucose disposal

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Explain the thermodynamic mechanism utilized by the SGLT-1 system to transport glucose into intestinal mucosal cells.
back:
* Secondary active transport
* Couples glucose entry against its gradient with Na+ moving down its gradient
* Na+ gradient maintained by basolateral Na+/K+ ATPase

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: A patient presents with a defect in the GLUT-2 transporter. Contrast the expected glycemic impact during the fed state versus the fasting state.
back:
* Fed state: Post-prandial hyperglycemia (impaired hepatic uptake)
* Fasting state: Fasting hypoglycemia (impaired release of glucose from liver)
* GLUT-2 is a bidirectional, high-capacity transporter

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: In addition to the liver, identify the specific pancreatic cell type and function where GLUT-2 serves as a high-Km 'glucose sensor'.
back:
* Pancreatic Beta Cells
* Functions as a sensor to trigger insulin secretion
* Only active when blood glucose levels are high

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: The specialized transporter responsible for the primary absorption of dietary fructose in the small intestinal mucosa is [___].
back:
* GLUT-5
* Sodium-independent facilitated diffusion
* Specific for fructose, not glucose
* Found in small intestine and testes

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: A neonate presents with severe osmotic diarrhea and dehydration immediately after beginning milk feeds. If the condition is a defect in SGLT-1, identify the two specific sugars whose absorption is impaired.
back:
* Glucose
* Galactose
* SGLT-1 transports both monosaccharides via Na+ co-transport
* Fructose absorption (GLUT-5) remains normal

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: In a patient with Type 1 Diabetes, explain how exercise can still promote glucose entry into skeletal muscle despite a lack of insulin.
back:
* Muscle contraction stimulates GLUT-4 translocation
* Occurs via insulin-independent signaling (AMPK pathway)
* Provides an alternative mechanism for glucose uptake during physical activity

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Distinguish between the GLUT family and the SGLT family regarding their energy requirements and direction of transport.
back:
* GLUTs: Facilitated diffusion; no ATP; down concentration gradient
* SGLTs: Secondary active transport; uses Na+ gradient energy; against concentration gradient

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Identify the primary glucose transporter utilized by neurons in the central nervous system to maintain high-affinity uptake.
back:
* GLUT-3
* High affinity, low Km
* Ensures preferential glucose uptake even during hypoglycemia
* Primarily neuronal distribution

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: The insulin-dependent glucose transporter, which is translocated from intracellular vesicles to the plasma membrane in response to insulin, is [___].
back:
• GLUT-4
• Predominantly located in skeletal muscle, cardiac muscle, and adipose tissue.
• Essential for post-prandial glucose uptake.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: A neonate presents with severe osmotic diarrhea and dehydration shortly after beginning breast milk. Stool analysis reveals unabsorbed glucose and galactose. This suggests a deficiency in which specific secondary active transport system?
back:
• SGLT-1 (Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 1)
• Transports glucose and galactose against their gradient.
• Driven by the Na+ gradient created by Na+/K+ ATPase.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: How does the Na+/K+ ATPase pump indirectly facilitate the intestinal absorption of glucose in the apical membrane of enterocytes?
back:
• Maintains low intracellular sodium concentration.
• Creates a steep downhill Na+ gradient.
• Powers SGLT-1 to pull glucose against its concentration gradient (Secondary Active Transport).

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
coreConcept: Differential roles of GLUT-2 and GLUT-4
front: Contrast the glucose-sensing role of GLUT-2 in pancreatic β-cells with the recruitment mechanism of GLUT-4 in skeletal muscle myocytes.
back:
• GLUT-2: High Km (low affinity); facilitates glucose entry proportional to blood levels to trigger insulin release.
• GLUT-4: Low Km; its density on the membrane is regulated by insulin/exercise-induced translocation.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Identify the unique facilitated diffusion transporter that exhibits high specificity for dietary fructose rather than glucose.
back:
• GLUT-5
• Located on the apical membrane of enterocytes in the small intestine and in spermatozoa.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: The high-affinity glucose transporter primary responsible for glucose entry into erythrocytes and across the blood-brain barrier is [___].
back:
• GLUT-1
• Low Km (approx. 1 mM).
• Provides basal glucose uptake even during fasting states.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: A child presents with hepatomegaly and fasting hypoglycemia. Lab results show glucose in the urine (glycosuria) despite normoglycemia. A defect in which bidirectional glucose transporter found in the liver and kidney is suspected?
back:
• GLUT-2 (Fanconi-Bickel Syndrome)
• Bidirectional transport for glucose entry/exit in hepatocytes.
• Also found in pancreatic beta cells and the basolateral membrane of enterocytes.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Explain the 'alternating access' model utilized by GLUT proteins to move glucose across the hydrophobic lipid bilayer.
back:
• Glucose binds to an outward-facing site on the GLUT protein.
• Transporter undergoes a reversible conformational change.
• Binding site shifts to an inward-facing state, releasing glucose into the cytosol.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Distinguish between SGLTs and GLUTs based on their energy requirement and direction of transport relative to the concentration gradient.
back:
• SGLTs: Secondary active transport; moves glucose against gradient using Na+ co-transport.
• GLUTs: Facilitated diffusion; moves glucose down gradient without energy consumption.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Name the primary glucose transporter isoform expressed in neurons to ensure consistent energy delivery to the CNS.
back:
• GLUT-3
• High-affinity transporter.
• Works in conjunction with GLUT-1 at the blood-brain barrier.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: In skeletal muscle and adipose tissue, the specific glucose transporter isoform that is sequestered in intracellular vesicles and translocated to the cell membrane in response to insulin is [___].
back: GLUT-4 is an insulin-dependent transporter. It is sequestered in vesicles and moves to the cell membrane when insulin levels rise, facilitating glucose uptake in muscle and adipose tissue.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: A newborn presents with severe osmotic diarrhea and dehydration shortly after starting a milk-based formula. Stool analysis reveals unabsorbed glucose and galactose. This condition likely involves a defect in [___].
back: SGLT-1 (Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 1). It mediates the active uptake of glucose and galactose from the intestinal lumen by coupling with the Na+ gradient to drive uphill transport.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Describe the secondary active transport mechanism utilized by SGLT-1 to move glucose against its concentration gradient into intestinal epithelial cells.
back: It couples the entry of glucose with Na+ ions. The Na+/K+ ATPase maintains a low intracellular Na+ concentration, providing the electrochemical gradient necessary for uphill glucose and galactose transport.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Contrast the glucose transport mechanisms in the brain (blood-brain barrier) versus the pancreatic beta cells during a period of fluctuating blood sugar levels.
back: The blood-brain barrier uses high-affinity GLUT-1 for constant glucose supply. Pancreatic beta cells use low-affinity GLUT-2, which allows for glucose sensing to regulate insulin secretion based on blood levels.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Specify the transporter primarily responsible for the facilitated diffusion of dietary fructose across the luminal membrane of the small intestine.
back: GLUT-5 is the specific transporter for fructose. It functions via Na+-independent facilitated diffusion and is primarily located in the small intestine and testes for fructose uptake.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: The high-capacity, low-affinity bidirectional glucose transporter that allows the liver to either take up glucose for glycogenesis or release it into the blood during fasting is [___].
back: GLUT-2 is the bidirectional transporter. It has a high capacity and low affinity, permitting the liver to manage blood glucose levels during both the well-fed and fasting states.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: A patient with uncontrolled hyperglycemia exceeds the renal threshold for glucose, resulting in glucosuria. The saturated transporters in the proximal renal tubules are [___].
back: SGLT transporters in the proximal tubule. These secondary active transporters reabsorb glucose from the filtrate until their transport maximum is exceeded during significant hyperglycemia.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Explain the role of GLUT-2 in the overall intestinal absorption of monosaccharides after they have entered the mucosal cell from the lumen.
back: GLUT-2 is located on the basolateral membrane of mucosal cells. It facilitates the movement of glucose, galactose, and fructose into the portal blood via Na+-independent facilitated diffusion down their gradients.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Distinguish between the transport of glucose into erythrocytes and the transport of glucose into neurons.
back: Erythrocytes primarily utilize GLUT-1 for high basal glucose uptake. Neurons utilize GLUT-3, which is the primary glucose transporter in neural tissue for efficient and rapid glucose uptake.

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Identify the primary anatomical locations where the Na+-monosaccharide cotransporter (SGLT) systems are found in the human body.
back: SGLT transporters are found in the luminal membrane of intestinal epithelial cells, the proximal tubules of the kidney, and the choroid plexus of the brain.

category: Give the composition and importance of pancreatic juice, bile and succus entericus and related clinical disorders (pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis, cholelithiasis)
front: The enzyme [___], secreted by the intestinal mucosa into the succus entericus, is the master activator that converts pancreatic trypsinogen into active trypsin.
back: Enteropeptidase (or Enterokinase). Found in succus entericus. Initiates the protein digestion cascade in the duodenum.

category: Give the composition and importance of pancreatic juice, bile and succus entericus and related clinical disorders (pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis, cholelithiasis)
front: A 45-year-old male with a history of gallstones presents with sudden, excruciating epigastric pain radiating to the back. The underlying biochemical event is the premature activation of [___] within the pancreas.
back: Trypsin. It leads to acinar cell autodigestion. Characterizes the onset of Acute Pancreatitis.

category: Give the composition and importance of pancreatic juice, bile and succus entericus and related clinical disorders (pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis, cholelithiasis)
front: Explain the diagnostic contrast between the composition of pancreatic juice during the cephalic phase versus the intestinal phase triggered by secretin.
back: Cephalic phase: Low volume, high enzyme content (vagal stimulus). Intestinal phase (Secretin): High volume, bicarbonate-rich, alkaline secretion (neutralizes acid).

category: Give the composition and importance of pancreatic juice, bile and succus entericus and related clinical disorders (pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis, cholelithiasis)
front: A 40-year-old patient presents with clay-colored stools and jaundice due to cholelithiasis. Contrast the fecal findings in this case with those expected in a patient with pancreatic insufficiency due to cystic fibrosis.
back: Cholelithiasis: Pale/clay stools (lack of stercobilin). Cystic Fibrosis: Greasy, foul-smelling steatorrhea (undigested fats due to lipase deficiency).

category: Give the composition and importance of pancreatic juice, bile and succus entericus and related clinical disorders (pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis, cholelithiasis)
front: Identify the pharmacological reason for administering a Proton Pump Inhibitor (PPI) as a step to enhance the effectiveness of oral pancreatic enzyme replacement in cystic fibrosis.
back: Prevents gastric acid from denaturing oral enzymes. Ensures duodenal pH remains alkaline for enzyme activity. Optimizes lipase function.

category: Give the composition and importance of pancreatic juice, bile and succus entericus and related clinical disorders (pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis, cholelithiasis)
front: The [___] test is the primary diagnostic criterion used to confirm the chloride transport defect characteristic of Cystic Fibrosis.
back: Sweat Chloride Test. Measures chloride levels in sweat. CF is confirmed if chloride is >60 mmol/L.

category: Give the composition and importance of pancreatic juice, bile and succus entericus and related clinical disorders (pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis, cholelithiasis)
front: A neonate with meconium ileus is suspected of having cystic fibrosis. Explain how the thick, viscid exocrine secretions in this concept contribute to intestinal obstruction.
back: Defective CFTR chloride channels lead to decreased water secretion. Pancreatic and intestinal juices become thick and dehydrated. Resulting viscid mucus causes plugging and obstruction.

category: Give the composition and importance of pancreatic juice, bile and succus entericus and related clinical disorders (pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis, cholelithiasis)
front: Detail the biochemical basis for why a patient with a complete bile duct obstruction develops steatorrhea despite having a healthy and functional pancreas.
back: Steatorrhea occurs due to a lack of bile salts. Prevents fat emulsification and micelle formation. Triglycerides cannot be efficiently absorbed without micelle transport.

category: Give the composition and importance of pancreatic juice, bile and succus entericus and related clinical disorders (pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis, cholelithiasis)
front: Contrast the physiological 'loop' of bile salts through the enterohepatic circulation with the fate of pancreatic enzymes after digestion is complete.
back: Bile Salts: 95% are reabsorbed in the terminal ileum and recycled to the liver. Pancreatic Enzymes: Digested by proteases or excreted in feces.

category: Give the composition and importance of pancreatic juice, bile and succus entericus and related clinical disorders (pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis, cholelithiasis)
front: Identify the primary enzyme found in pancreatic juice responsible for starch hydrolysis and the specific inorganic ion required for its activation.
back: Amylopsin (Pancreatic alpha-Amylase). Requires Chloride (Cl-) ions for activation. Hydrolyzes alpha-1,4 linkages of starch.

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: The primary anabolic hormone that facilitates glucose uptake into skeletal muscle and adipose tissue via the translocation of GLUT-4 transporters is [___].
back:
• Insulin
• Secreted by pancreatic β-cells
• Stimulates glycogenesis and glycolysis
• Inhibits gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: A 45-year-old patient with an adrenal cortex tumor presents with hyperglycemia and muscle wasting. Excessive secretion of [___] is promoting hepatic gluconeogenesis and peripheral insulin resistance.
back:
• Cortisol (Glucocorticoids)
• Stimulates amino acid mobilization from muscle
• Induces PEP-carboxykinase gene expression
• Antagonizes insulin action in peripheral tissues

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: Explain the role of Epinephrine in the 'Fight or Flight' response regarding carbohydrate fuel mobilization.
back:
• Rapidly stimulates hepatic and muscle glycogenolysis
• Increases glucagon secretion and inhibits insulin release
• Acts via β-adrenergic receptors and cAMP pathway
• Provides immediate glucose for exercising muscle

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: Contrast the hyperglycemic mechanisms of Glucagon and Cortisol during prolonged fasting.
back:
• Glucagon: Rapidly activates hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis via cAMP/PKA signaling
• Cortisol: Slower response; increases enzyme synthesis (PEPCK) and provides substrate via muscle proteolysis

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: Describe the physiological significance of the Incretin hormones (GLP-1 and GIP) in glucose homeostasis.
back:
• Secreted by the gut in response to oral glucose
• Potentiate insulin secretion (the Incretin Effect)
• Suppress inappropriate glucagon secretion post-prandially
• Slow gastric emptying to prevent glucose spikes

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: The pancreatic hormone that acts as a paracrine inhibitor, suppressing the secretion of both insulin and glucagon to modulate carbohydrate flux, is [___].
back:
• Somatostatin
• Secreted by δ-cells (delta cells)
• Prevents rapid exhaustion of nutrients
• Extends the period of nutrient absorption

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: A patient with a pituitary somatotroph adenoma exhibits persistent hyperglycemia. Identify the hormone responsible and its primary metabolic effect.
back:
• Growth Hormone (GH)
• Decreases peripheral glucose uptake (anti-insulin effect)
• Stimulates gluconeogenesis in the liver
• Promotes lipolysis to provide alternative fuel

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
coreConcept: Hormonal Control of the Bifunctional Enzyme
front: Detail the molecular mechanism by which Glucagon overrides Glycolysis in favor of Gluconeogenesis in the liver.
back:
• Activates cAMP-dependent Protein Kinase A
• Phosphorylates PFK-2/FBP-2 bifunctional enzyme
• Decreases Fructose 2,6-bisphosphate levels
• Relieves inhibition of Fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: Distinguish between the effects of Glucagon and Epinephrine on skeletal muscle glycogen stores.
back:
• Epinephrine: Stimulates glycogenolysis in muscle (via β-receptors)
• Glucagon: No effect on muscle glycogen due to lack of specific receptors
• Glucagon acts strictly on hepatic glycogen

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: Which pancreatic hormone is primarily responsible for preventing hypoglycemia during a protein-rich meal by stimulating hepatic glucose output?
back:
• Glucagon
• Stimulated by amino acids (arginine/alanine)
• Offsets insulin-induced hypoglycemia after protein ingestion
• Maintains euglycemia during non-carbohydrate meals

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: The pancreatic hormone produced by alpha cells that acts as a primary counter-regulatory agent to insulin by stimulating hepatic glycogenolysis is [___].
back: Glucagon; Secreted by pancreatic alpha cells; Stimulates glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis; Increases blood glucose levels during fasting.

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: A 50-year-old patient presents with a 'Somatostatinoma' (a D-cell tumor). Why does this patient frequently develop secondary Diabetes Mellitus?
back: Excess somatostatin inhibits insulin secretion; Acts via paracrine/endocrine pathways; Inhibits both insulin and glucagon release; Causes glucose intolerance.

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: Explain the role of Gastric Inhibitory Peptide (GIP) as an incretin in the regulation of carbohydrate metabolism.
back: Secreted by duodenal K-cells; Stimulates insulin release; Triggered by oral glucose; Enhances postprandial glucose clearance.

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
coreConcept: Insulin as the Primary Hypoglycemic Hormone
front: The primary anabolic hormone produced by the $\beta$-cells of the pancreas that lowers blood glucose levels is [___].
back:
Insulin.
- Increases glucose uptake in muscle/adipose via GLUT-4.
- Stimulates glycolysis and glycogenesis.
- Inhibits gluconeogenesis.

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: A 50-year-old patient on long-term high-dose dexamethasone therapy develops new-onset hyperglycemia. Which physiological mechanism of this hormone class is responsible?
back:
Glucocorticoid-induced gluconeogenesis.
- Induces transcription of PEPCK.
- Promotes amino acid mobilization from muscle.
- Decreases peripheral glucose utilization.

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: How does glucagon acutely increase blood glucose levels during the fasting state via hepatic action?
back:
- Binds G-protein coupled receptors.
- Increases cAMP/Protein Kinase A.
- Activates glycogen phosphorylase (glycogenolysis).
- Inhibits glycogen synthase.

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: Contrast the metabolic destination of glucose mobilized by epinephrine in skeletal muscle versus the liver.
back:
Liver: Releases free glucose into blood (expresses Glucose 6-phosphatase).
Muscle: Glucose 6-P enters glycolysis for ATP production (lacks Glucose 6-phosphatase).

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: Identify the pancreatic $\delta$-cell hormone that functions as a universal inhibitor of both insulin and glucagon secretion.
back:
Somatostatin.
- Acts via paracrine signaling.
- Decreases the rate of nutrient absorption and gastric emptying.

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: In the presence of an anterior pituitary tumor secreting excess [___], patients often develop insulin resistance and secondary 'pituitary diabetes'.
back:
Growth Hormone (GH).
- Antagonizes insulin action (diabetogenic effect).
- Decreases glucose uptake in peripheral tissues.
- Increases lipolysis.

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: A patient presents with tachycardia and tremors. Lab work shows hyperthyroidism and a slightly elevated fasting blood glucose. Explain the hormonal effect on carbohydrate absorption.
back: Thyroid hormones (T3/T4) increase the rate of glucose absorption from the gastrointestinal tract, contributing to postprandial hyperglycemia.

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: Explain the specific intracellular mechanism by which insulin facilitates glucose entry into myocytes.
back:
- Binds Tyrosine Kinase receptor.
- Triggers signaling cascade.
- Causes translocation of GLUT-4 vesicles to the plasma membrane.

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
coreConcept: Hormonal Control of Glycolysis vs Gluconeogenesis
front: Distinguish the metabolic roles of Insulin and Glucagon regarding the regulation of the bifunctional enzyme PFK-2/FBP-2 in the liver.
back:
Insulin: Dephosphorylates enzyme $\rightarrow$ Increases F-2,6-BP $\rightarrow$ Stimulates Glycolysis.
Glucagon: Phosphorylates enzyme $\rightarrow$ Decreases F-2,6-BP $\rightarrow$ Stimulates Gluconeogenesis.

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: Enlist the four major counter-regulatory hormones that prevent hypoglycemia by opposing insulin action.
back:
1. Glucagon
2. Epinephrine
3. Cortisol
4. Growth Hormone

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: The primary glucose transporter isoform that is translocated to the cell membrane in an insulin-dependent manner in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue is [___].
back:
- GLUT-4
- Regulated by insulin signaling
- Found in cardiac muscle, skeletal muscle, and adipocytes

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: A neonate presents with persistent hypoglycemia. Investigations reveal a defect in the 'glucose sensor' protein of the pancreatic beta cells and liver hepatocytes. Identify the protein.
back:
- GLUT-2
- High Km (low affinity) and high Vmax
- Functions as a glucose sensor in beta cells and facilitates liver glucose output

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Explain how SGLT-1 facilitates the entry of glucose and galactose into the intestinal mucosal cells against their concentration gradients.
back:
- Secondary active transport
- Uses energy from the Na+ gradient established by Na+/K+ ATPase
- Cotransports 2 Na+ ions with 1 sugar molecule

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Contrast the glucose transport mechanism at the apical (luminal) membrane vs. the basolateral membrane of a small intestine enterocyte.
back:
- Apical: SGLT-1 (Secondary active transport; Na+-dependent)
- Basolateral: GLUT-2 (Facilitated diffusion; Na+-independent)
- SGLT-1 concentrates glucose; GLUT-2 releases it into portal blood

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: State the glucose transporter isoform characterized by the highest affinity for glucose, ensuring priority supply to neurons in the brain.
back:
- GLUT-3
- Low Km value
- Facilitates continuous glucose uptake even during low systemic concentrations

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: The specialized, Na+-independent transporter located in the small intestine and testes that primarily facilitates the facilitated diffusion of fructose is [___].
back:
- GLUT-5
- Specific for fructose absorption
- Does not transport glucose or galactose effectively

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: A child presents with severe osmotic diarrhea and dehydration. Tests confirm a total failure of the Na+-dependent uptake of glucose and galactose. Which specific transporter is affected?
back:
- SGLT-1
- Pathophysiology: Glucose-Galactose Malabsorption
- Unabsorbed sugars cause osmotic water draw and bacterial fermentation

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Detail the signaling pathway triggered by insulin that leads to the rapid increase in glucose uptake in adipocytes.
back:
- Insulin binds Tyrosine Kinase receptor
- Activates PI3K/Akt pathway
- Triggers translocation of GLUT-4 containing vesicles to the plasma membrane

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Distinguish between the GLUT family and the SGLT family of transporters regarding their requirement for metabolic energy.
back:
- GLUT: Passive (Facilitated diffusion); no energy required
- SGLT: Active (Secondary active transport); requires Na+/K+ ATPase energy
- GLUT follows gradient; SGLT can move sugars against gradient

category: Elaborate key features of various transport systems for entry of glucose into cells
front: Identify the glucose transporter isoform that provides basal glucose uptake for red blood cells and the blood-brain barrier.
back:
- GLUT-1
- Found in erythrocytes and brain microvessels
- High affinity to ensure steady basal glucose supply

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: The gastrointestinal hormone primarily responsible for stimulating the secretion of bicarbonate-rich pancreatic juice in response to acidic chyme is [___].
back:
• Secretin
• Produced by S cells in the duodenum
• Neutralizes gastric acid to provide an optimal pH for pancreatic enzymes.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: A 45-year-old male with recurrent peptic ulcers is found to have a gastrinoma (Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome). Explain the primary metabolic effect of excess Gastrin on the stomach.
back:
• Massive stimulation of HCl secretion
• Acts on parietal cell receptors
• Indirectly triggers histamine release from ECL cells
• Causes hyperplasia of the gastric mucosa.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: Describe the mechanism by which Cholecystokinin (CCK) facilitates the metabolic digestion of fats and proteins in the small intestine.
back:
• Stimulates pancreatic acinar cells to release digestive enzymes
• Causes gallbladder contraction and Sphincter of Oddi relaxation
• Inhibits gastric emptying to allow time for digestion.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: A patient presents with high gastric acidity. Contrast the metabolic roles of Gastrin and Somatostatin in regulating this physiological state.
back:
• Gastrin: Stimulates HCl production via H2-mediated pathways.
• Somatostatin: Potent inhibitor; suppresses G-cells, ECL cells, and parietal cells.
• Somatostatin acts as a 'metabolic brake' when luminal pH falls below 2.0.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: Identify the pharmacological target of Omeprazole and its specific role in the final step of the gastric metabolic pathway.
back:
• Targets the H+/K+ ATPase (Proton Pump)
• Located on the apical membrane of parietal cells
• Irreversibly inhibits the active transport of H+ into the gastric lumen.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: In the intestinal phase of gastric secretion, the inhibitory effect of fats is mediated by a group of hormones collectively known as [___].
back:
• Enterogastrones (GIP, Secretin, CCK)
• Inhibits gastric acid secretion
• Decreases gastric motility to manage chyme volume in the duodenum.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: A patient with severe watery diarrhea and hypokalemia is diagnosed with a VIPoma. Explain the metabolic effect of Vasoactive Intestinal Peptide (VIP) on intestinal transport.
back:
• Stimulates secretion of water and electrolytes into the lumen
• Increases intestinal cAMP levels
• Relaxes intestinal smooth muscle and sphincters
• Inhibits gastrin-stimulated acid secretion.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: Explain why the metabolic insulin response is significantly higher when glucose is administered orally compared to an equivalent intravenous dose.
back:
• Mediated by Incretins (GIP and GLP-1)
• Secreted by gut K and L cells in response to luminal glucose
• Directly stimulate pancreatic beta-cells to enhance insulin release before blood glucose rises.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: Distinguish between the primary metabolic triggers for the release of Secretin versus Cholecystokinin (CCK) in the duodenum.
back:
• Secretin: Triggered by low pH (<4.5) in the duodenal lumen.
• CCK: Triggered by fatty acids and amino acids/peptides.
• Secretin manages acidity; CCK manages nutrient processing.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: Identify the enzyme within parietal cells responsible for providing the H+ ions used in the metabolic production of Hydrochloric Acid.
back:
• Carbonic Anhydrase
• Catalyzes: CO2 + H2O → H2CO3 → H+ + HCO3-
• The H+ is pumped into the lumen; HCO3- enters blood (alkaline tide).

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: The only hypoglycemic hormone secreted by the B-cells of the islets of Langerhans is [___].
back: Insulin. 1. Lowers blood glucose by increasing uptake via GLUT-4 in muscle and adipose. 2. Stimulates glycogenesis. 3. Inhibits gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis.

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: A patient with a tumor of the adrenal medulla (Pheochromocytoma) exhibits persistent hyperglycemia. This is primarily due to the overproduction of [___].
back: Epinephrine (Adrenaline). 1. Stimulates rapid hepatic glycogenolysis. 2. Inhibits insulin secretion via alpha-2 receptors. 3. Promotes glucagon release to sustain glucose levels.

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: Explain the primary mechanism by which Glucagon prevents hypoglycemia during the fasting state.
back: 1. Activates adenylate cyclase to stimulate hepatic glycogenolysis. 2. Promotes gluconeogenesis from amino acids and lactate. 3. Mobilizes fatty acids as an alternative fuel source.

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: Contrast the effects of Cortisol versus Growth Hormone (GH) on peripheral glucose utilization.
back: 1. Cortisol: Decreases glucose uptake and promotes insulin resistance while stimulating gluconeogenesis. 2. GH: Decreases glucose uptake in muscle (anti-insulin effect) and stimulates lipolysis. 3. Both are diabetogenic.

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: Name the paracrine hormone that inhibits both insulin and glucagon secretion to locally modulate carbohydrate metabolism.
back: Somatostatin (D-cells). 1. Decreases the rate of nutrient absorption from the GIT. 2. Inhibits secretion of insulin, glucagon, and GH. 3. Reduces splanchnic blood flow.

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: In the diagnosis of Cushing's Syndrome, hyperglycemia and 'steroid diabetes' are caused by excessive secretion of [___].
back: Cortisol (Glucocorticoids). 1. Increases expression of PEPCK for gluconeogenesis. 2. Decreases peripheral glucose utilization. 3. Enhances liver glycogen storage (paradoxical effect).

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: A 45-year-old male with acromegaly presents with impaired glucose tolerance. Identify the hormone responsible and its effect on hepatic glucose output.
back: Growth Hormone (GH). 1. Increases hepatic glucose output. 2. Impairs insulin-mediated suppression of gluconeogenesis. 3. Leads to secondary diabetes mellitus in chronic excess.

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: Detail the mechanism by which Thyroid hormones (T3/T4) contribute to the hyperglycemic state in hyperthyroid patients.
back: 1. Increases rate of intestinal glucose absorption. 2. Sensitizes tissues to catecholamines. 3. Accelerates hepatic insulin degradation and increases glycogenolysis.

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: Contrast the roles of Insulin and Glucagon in the regulation of the metabolic switch enzyme Fructose 2,6-bisphosphate.
back: 1. Insulin: Increases F2,6-BP, stimulating glycolysis via PFK-1. 2. Glucagon: Decreases F2,6-BP by activating FBPase-2, stimulating gluconeogenesis. 3. Occurs via cAMP-dependent protein kinase A phosphorylation.

category: Enlist the hormones that play important roles in regulating carbohydrate metabolism
front: Enlist the three primary catecholamine-mediated actions that raise blood sugar during an acute 'fight or flight' response.
back: 1. Stimulation of hepatic and muscle glycogenolysis. 2. Direct inhibition of insulin release from the pancreas. 3. Stimulation of glucagon secretion to maintain glucose supply.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: The hormone primarily responsible for stimulating the secretion of bicarbonate-rich pancreatic juice in response to duodenal acidity is [___].
back: * Secretin. * Released by S-cells in the duodenum. * Acts on pancreatic ductal cells. * Neutralizes acidic gastric chyme.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: A patient presents with epigastric pain and high serum gastrin levels. Investigation reveals a gastrin-secreting tumor. State the primary effect of this hormone on parietal cells.
back: * Stimulates HCl production. * Acts directly on gastrin receptors. * Triggers histamine release from ECL cells. * Leads to peptic ulceration in Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: Explain how Cholecystokinin (CCK) facilitates the digestion of macronutrients in the small intestine.
back: * Stimulates pancreatic acinar cells to release enzymes. * Triggers gallbladder contraction. * Relaxes the Sphincter of Oddi. * Slows gastric emptying to allow time for digestion.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: Contrast the physiological triggers and primary pancreatic targets of Secretin versus Cholecystokinin (CCK).
back: * Triggers: Secretin by acid (H+); CCK by fat/protein products. * Targets: Secretin acts on ductal cells (HCO3-); CCK acts on acinar cells (digestive enzymes).

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: Describe the inhibitory role of Enterogastrones like Gastric Inhibitory Peptide (GIP) on gastric function.
back: * Inhibits gastric acid (HCl) secretion. * Decreases gastric motility. * Released from the proximal small intestine. * Primarily triggered by the presence of fat in the duodenum.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: The hormone [___], released by D cells, acts as a potent universal inhibitor of both gastrin and hydrochloric acid secretion.
back: * Somatostatin. * Provides paracrine and endocrine inhibition. * Reduces gastric acid production. * Responds to high intraluminal acidity.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: Following a high-protein meal, a significant rise in gastric acid is noted. Identify the hormonal mediator and its specific cellular source in the stomach.
back: * Hormone: Gastrin. * Source: G cells. * Location: Pyloric antrum. * Trigger: Amino acids (phenylalanine and tryptophan) and stomach distension.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: Detail the specific intracellular signaling pathways utilized by CCK and Secretin to induce pancreatic secretion.
back: * CCK: Uses Phospholipase C pathway (increases IP3/DAG and intracellular Ca2+). * Secretin: Uses Adenylyl cyclase pathway (increases cAMP levels). * Drives enzyme and fluid secretion respectively.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: Distinguish between the metabolic effects of Vasoactive Intestinal Polypeptide (VIP) and Acetylcholine on salivary gland activity.
back: * Acetylcholine: Directly stimulates acinar cell secretion. * VIP: Functions as a cotransmitter causing marked local vasodilation. * Both work together to increase total salivary flow.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: Name the primary physiological stimulant for the release of Secretin into the bloodstream.
back: * Presence of hydrochloric acid (H+). * Contact of chyme with pH <4.5 with duodenal S-cells. * Results in the release of alkaline pancreatic and biliary juice.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: In response to acidic chyme entering the duodenum, S-cells release the hormone [___], which primarily stimulates the secretion of bicarbonate-rich pancreatic juice.
back: • Secretin. • Neutralizes gastric HCl in the duodenum. • Creates an alkaline environment (pH 8.0-8.3) necessary for pancreatic enzyme activity. • Inhibits further Gastrin release.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: A patient experiences postprandial right-upper-quadrant pain after a fatty meal. The hormone responsible for gallbladder contraction and the secretion of viscid, enzyme-rich pancreatic juice is [___].
back: • Cholecystokinin (CCK). • Produced by I-cells in the duodenum and jejunum. • Stimulated by long-chain fatty acids and peptides. • Acts via Phospholipase C to increase intracellular calcium in acinar cells.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: Contrast the metabolic effects of Gastrin and Secretin on gastric acid (HCl) secretion and duodenal pH regulation.
back: • Gastrin: Potently stimulates HCl secretion from parietal cells and increases gastric motility. • Secretin: Inhibits HCl secretion and promotes bicarbonate release. • Gastrin decreases stomach pH, while Secretin increases duodenal pH for enzyme function.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: The gastrointestinal hormone secreted by S cells in response to a low duodenal pH that primarily stimulates the release of bicarbonate-rich pancreatic juice is [___].
back: Secretin. • Neutralizes acidic chyme in the duodenum. • Inhibits gastric HCl secretion and motility. • Stimulates pepsinogen secretion from chief cells.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: A medical student consumes a meal rich in phenylalanine and tryptophan. These amino acids stimulate the release of [___] from the G cells to increase gastric acid secretion.
back: Gastrin. • Secreted by G cells in the pyloric antrum. • Stimulates HCl production by acting on parietal and Histamine-releasing ECL cells.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: Explain the primary biological role of Cholecystokinin (CCK) regarding pancreatic acinar cells and the gallbladder.
back: • Stimulates pancreatic acinar cells to produce enzyme-rich juice. • Causes gallbladder contraction and relaxation of the Sphincter of Oddi to facilitate bile flow.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: Contrast the pancreatic juice composition secreted in response to Secretin versus that secreted in response to Cholecystokinin (CCK).
back: • Secretin: High-volume, watery secretion rich in bicarbonate (HCO3-). • CCK: Low-volume, viscous secretion rich in digestive enzymes.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: Identify the hormone released by D cells in the stomach and explain its primary metabolic effect on acid production.
back: Somatostatin. • Acts as a universal inhibitor. • Decreases HCl secretion by directly inhibiting parietal cells and indirectly inhibiting gastrin/histamine release.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
front: Fatty acids in the duodenum trigger the release of [___], a hormone that prevents gastric overfilling by inhibiting both gastric acid secretion and motility.
back: GIP (Gastric Inhibitory Peptide). • Member of the enterogastrone family. • Inhibits gastric secretory and motor activities in response to fat.

category: Elaborate the metabolic effects of these hormones
