* Glycerol is phosphorylated to Glycerol 3-phosphate by Glycerol Kinase.
* Oxidized to Dihydroxyacetone phosphate (DHAP).
* Enters the gluconeogenic pathway as a triose phosphate intermediate.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Contrast the metabolic fate of pyruvate in the liver during a state of high Acetyl CoA accumulation (e.g., during starvation).
back:
* Acetyl CoA allosterically inhibits Pyruvate Dehydrogenase (blocking TCA cycle entry).
* Acetyl CoA allosterically activates Pyruvate Carboxylase.
* This diverts pyruvate toward Oxaloacetate and subsequent glucose synthesis.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Identify the primary rate-limiting enzyme of gluconeogenesis and the two specific intracellular molecules that act as its potent allosteric inhibitors.
back:
* Enzyme: Fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase.
* Inhibitors: Fructose 2,6-bisphosphate and AMP.
* This prevents a futile cycle with Phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK-1).

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: The conversion of pyruvate to oxaloacetate, the first step of gluconeogenesis, is catalyzed by the enzyme [___] which requires biotin as a coenzyme.
back: * Pyruvate carboxylase. * Occurs within the mitochondria. * Allosterically activated by Acetyl-CoA.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: A chronic alcoholic presents with profound fasting hypoglycemia after a binge. Explain the biochemical effect of an elevated NADH/NAD+ ratio on gluconeogenic precursors.
back: * Drives OAA to malate reduction. * Drives pyruvate to lactate reduction. * Diverts essential substrates away from glucose synthesis.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Describe the shuttle mechanism used to transport mitochondrial oxaloacetate (OAA) into the cytosol for the completion of gluconeogenesis.
back: * OAA reduced to Malate by mitochondrial MDH. * Malate crosses the mitochondrial membrane. * Malate re-oxidized to OAA by cytosolic MDH.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: A child presents with growth failure and hepatomegaly. Labs show fasting hypoglycemia and lactic acidosis. If the bypass of the pyruvate kinase step is defective, the most likely enzyme deficiency is [___].
back: * PEP Carboxykinase (PEPCK) or Pyruvate Carboxylase. * Blocks conversion of pyruvate/OAA to PEP. * Forces pyruvate into lactate production.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Specify the role of Acetyl-CoA as an allosteric regulator in shifting metabolism from the TCA cycle to gluconeogenesis during a fast.
back: * Potent activator of Pyruvate Carboxylase. * Inhibitor of Pyruvate Dehydrogenase (PDH). * Ensures pyruvate is used for OAA synthesis.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: The final hydrolytic step of gluconeogenesis that releases free glucose into the blood occurs in the [___] (organelle) of hepatocytes.
back: * Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER). * Catalyzed by Glucose 6-phosphatase. * Transporters (T1, T2, T3) move substrates/products.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: An infant with Type Ia Glycogen Storage Disease cannot release glucose from the liver. Explain why this patient remains hypoglycemic despite intact gluconeogenic pathways to Glucose-6-P.
back: * Deficiency of Glucose 6-phosphatase. * Common final step for both glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis. * Glucose remains trapped as G-6-P.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Explain the reciprocal regulation of Fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase and PFK-1 by Fructose 2,6-bisphosphate in the liver.
back: * F2,6-BP inhibits F1,6-BPase (stops gluconeogenesis). * F2,6-BP activates PFK-1 (starts glycolysis). * Glucagon lowers F2,6-BP to favor gluconeogenesis.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Contrast the gluconeogenic entry points of Glycerol versus Propionate (from odd-chain fatty acids).
back: * Glycerol: Enters as DHAP (Dihydroxyacetone phosphate). * Propionate: Enters as Succinyl-CoA (TCA intermediate). * Both bypass the initial pyruvate steps.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Identify the specific nucleotide triphosphate required by Phosphoenolpyruvate Carboxykinase (PEPCK) to convert oxaloacetate into phosphoenolpyruvate.
back: * Guanosine triphosphate (GTP). * Provides energy for simultaneous decarboxylation and phosphorylation. * Occurs in both mitochondria and cytosol.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: The enzyme Pyruvate Carboxylase, responsible for the initial bypass reaction in gluconeogenesis, requires the prosthetic group [___] to activate and transfer CO2 to pyruvate.
back:
• Biotin (Vitamin B7).
• Covalently attached to a lysine residue.
• Requires ATP for the formation of the enzyme-biotin-CO2 intermediate.
• Directs pyruvate into the oxaloacetate pool.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: A 4-month-old infant presents with tremors, night sweats, and massive hepatomegaly. Lab tests reveal severe fasting hypoglycemia and lactic acidosis. Biopsy shows normal glycogen structure but an inability to release free glucose into the blood. Identify the deficient enzyme.
back:
• Glucose 6-phosphatase.
• Located in the Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER).
• Final common step for both gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis.
• Pathophysiology of Von Gierke Disease (Type Ia GSD).

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Explain the regulatory mechanism by which high mitochondrial Acetyl CoA, produced during fasting-induced lipolysis, promotes glucose synthesis while inhibiting its oxidation.
back:
• Allosterically activates Pyruvate Carboxylase.
• Allosterically inhibits Pyruvate Dehydrogenase (PDH) Complex.
• Diverts pyruvate toward oxaloacetate for gluconeogenesis.
• Signals an energy-rich state favoring glucose production.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Contrast the regulatory effect of Fructose 2,6-bisphosphate on the gluconeogenic enzyme Fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase versus its glycolytic counterpart Phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK-1).
back:
• Fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase: Potently inhibited by F2,6-BP.
• PFK-1: Potently activated by F2,6-BP.
• This reciprocal regulation prevents a 'futile cycle'.
• Glucagon decreases F2,6-BP, thus activating gluconeogenesis.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Describe the biochemical steps required to utilize glycerol, released from adipose triacylglycerol hydrolysis, as a substrate for hepatic gluconeogenesis.
back:
• Phosphorylation: Glycerol to Glycerol 3-P via Glycerol Kinase.
• Oxidation: Glycerol 3-P to Dihydroxyacetone Phosphate (DHAP).
• Enzyme: Glycerol 3-phosphate dehydrogenase (NAD+ dependent).
• DHAP enters the pathway at the triose level.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: While the liver is the primary gluconeogenic organ during an overnight fast, the [___] becomes a major contributor during prolonged starvation, providing approximately 40% of the total glucose production.
back:
• Kidney (Renal Cortex).
• Possesses Glucose 6-phosphatase.
• Uses lactate and glutamine as primary substrates.
• Vital for glucose homeostasis in chronic fasting.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: A marathon runner exhibits elevated blood lactate levels. Detail the metabolic 'salvage' loop that allows this lactate to be converted back into glucose to maintain blood sugar.
back:
• The Cori Cycle.
• Lactate diffuses to liver via blood.
• Liver LDH oxidizes lactate to pyruvate.
• Pyruvate enters gluconeogenesis to form blood glucose for muscle use.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Delineate the sequence of events mitochondrial oxaloacetate must undergo to reach the cytosol for further processing by PEP-carboxykinase (PEPCK).
back:
• Reduction: OAA to Malate via Mitochondrial Malate Dehydrogenase.
• Transport: Malate crosses mitochondrial membrane via shuttle.
• Oxidation: Malate to OAA in cytosol via Cytosolic MDH.
• Indirectly transfers NADH required for gluconeogenesis.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Distinguish between glucogenic and ketogenic substrates in terms of their ability to provide a net gain of glucose in humans.
back:
• Glucogenic (e.g., Alanine, Glycerol): Yield pyruvate or TCA intermediates; net glucose gain.
• Ketogenic (e.g., Acetyl CoA, Leucine): Yield only Acetyl CoA; no net glucose gain.
• Reason: PDH reaction is irreversible.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Summarize the total high-energy phosphate bond cost (ATP and GTP) required to synthesize one molecule of glucose starting from two molecules of pyruvate.
back:
• Total: 6 high-energy bonds.
• 4 ATP: 2 at Pyruvate Carboxylase; 2 at Phosphoglycerate Kinase.
• 2 GTP: Used by PEP-carboxykinase (PEPCK).
• Note: 2 NADH are also consumed.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: The first step of gluconeogenesis involves the carboxylation of pyruvate to oxaloacetate in the mitochondria, a reaction requiring the coenzyme [___].
back:
• Biotin.
• Covalently bound to a lysine residue of pyruvate carboxylase.
• Requires ATP and CO2 to form the intermediate.
• Activated by Acetyl CoA.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: A child presents with severe fasting hypoglycemia, lactic acidosis, and hepatomegaly. Biopsy shows normal glycogen structure but an inability to export glucose from the liver. Which enzyme is likely defective?
back:
• Glucose 6-phosphatase.
• Located in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane.
• Required for the final step of both gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis.
• Deficiency causes Von Gierke disease.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Describe how high intramitochondrial levels of Acetyl CoA direct the metabolic fate of pyruvate during a fasting state.
back:
• Allosterically activates Pyruvate Carboxylase to produce OAA.
• Inhibits Pyruvate Dehydrogenase (via PDH kinase).
• Diverts pyruvate away from the TCA cycle toward gluconeogenesis.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Contrast the metabolic limitations of adipose tissue and the liver regarding the utilization of glycerol released during triacylglycerol hydrolysis.
back:
• Liver: Contains Glycerol Kinase; converts glycerol to DHAP for gluconeogenesis.
• Adipose: Lacks Glycerol Kinase; must release glycerol into the blood for hepatic processing.
• This ensures central glucose production during fasting.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Identify the specific high-energy molecule required by Phosphoenolpyruvate Carboxykinase (PEPCK) to convert oxaloacetate into phosphoenolpyruvate.
back:
• GTP (Guanosine Triphosphate).
• Provides the phosphate group and energy for decarboxylation.
• This step bypasses the irreversible pyruvate kinase reaction of glycolysis.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: During prolonged starvation (weeks), the organ responsible for approximately 40% of total glucose synthesis to assist the liver is the [___].
back:
• Kidney.
• While the liver provides 90% during overnight fasting, the renal cortex becomes a major contributor during chronic starvation.
• Helps maintain brain glucose requirements.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: A chronic alcoholic presents with fasting hypoglycemia. Explain the biochemical reason why an increased NADH:NAD+ ratio inhibits the entry of lactate into gluconeogenesis.
back:
• High NADH shifts the Lactate Dehydrogenase equilibrium toward Lactate.
• Prevents conversion of Lactate to Pyruvate.
• Similarly reduces OAA to Malate, depleting substrates for glucose synthesis.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Explain the mechanism by which intramitochondrial oxaloacetate reaches the cytosol to participate in the PEPCK reaction.
back:
• Malate Shuttle.
• OAA is reduced to Malate to cross the inner mitochondrial membrane.
• Cytosolic Malate Dehydrogenase re-oxidizes Malate back to OAA, generating NADH for gluconeogenesis.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Distinguish between the Cori Cycle and the Glucose-Alanine Cycle regarding the nitrogenous waste produced in the liver.
back:
• Cori Cycle: No nitrogen involved; involves lactate-glucose recycling.
• Glucose-Alanine Cycle: Alanine brings amino groups to the liver.
• Results in Urea production in the liver alongside glucose synthesis.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Identify the potent allosteric effector that decreases during fasting to allow the activation of Fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase-1.
back:
• Fructose 2,6-bisphosphate.
• Its synthesis is inhibited by glucagon (via cAMP/PKA).
• Low levels relieve inhibition of gluconeogenesis and prevent simultaneous glycolysis (reciprocal regulation).

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: The initial step of gluconeogenesis occurs in the mitochondria, where pyruvate is converted into oxaloacetate by the enzyme [___], which requires biotin as a coenzyme.
back:
Pyruvate Carboxylase.
• Catalyzes ATP-dependent carboxylation.
• Requires Biotin (Vitamin B7) and CO2.
• Allosterically activated by Acetyl CoA to signal high energy availability.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: A 10-month-old infant presents with hepatomegaly and hypoglycemia that does not improve with fructose administration. Lab tests show elevated lactate and glycerol. This suggests a deficiency in [___].
back:
Fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase.
• Key regulatory bypass of Phosphofructokinase-1.
• Inhibited by AMP and Fructose 2,6-bisphosphate.
• Deficiency prevents glucose synthesis from most non-carbohydrate substrates.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Explain the essential mechanism by which mitochondrial oxaloacetate (OAA) is made available for cytosolic gluconeogenic reactions.
back:
• OAA cannot cross the inner mitochondrial membrane.
• Reduced to Malate via mitochondrial Malate Dehydrogenase.
• Malate exits to the cytosol via a specific transporter.
• Re-oxidized to OAA via cytosolic Malate Dehydrogenase.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: A patient with uncontrolled diabetes is metabolizing fatty acids, producing excess Acetyl CoA. Contrast why this Acetyl CoA cannot be used for net glucose synthesis while Glycerol can.
back:
• Acetyl CoA: PDH reaction is irreversible; carbons exit TCA as CO2.
• Glycerol: Phosphorylated to Glycerol-3-P, then oxidized to Dihydroxyacetone Phosphate (DHAP).
• DHAP directly enters the gluconeogenic bypass pool.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Delineate the specific high-energy phosphate requirements for the synthesis of one molecule of glucose from two molecules of pyruvate.
back:
• 4 ATP: (2 for Pyruvate Carboxylase; 2 for Phosphoglycerate Kinase).
• 2 GTP: (for Phosphoenolpyruvate Carboxykinase).
• Total cost: 6 High-energy phosphate bonds per glucose molecule.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: The final step of gluconeogenesis, producing free glucose, is catalyzed by [___], which is uniquely localized in the membrane of the endoplasmic reticulum.
back:
Glucose 6-phosphatase.
• Bypasses the Hexokinase/Glucokinase reaction.
• Primarily localized in Liver and Kidney ER.
• Deficiency leads to Von Gierke disease (GSD Type Ia).

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: During high-intensity anaerobic exercise, an athlete's muscles produce lactate. Describe the metabolic route that allows this substrate to be recycled into blood glucose.
back:
Cori Cycle.
• Lactate diffuses into blood and enters the liver.
• Liver oxidizes Lactate to Pyruvate (LDH).
• Pyruvate enters gluconeogenesis to form Glucose.
• Glucose is released back to muscle.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Detail the conversion pathway of propionate, derived from odd-chain fatty acid oxidation, into the gluconeogenic precursor pool.
back:
• Propionate → Propionyl CoA.
• Propionyl CoA → Methylmalonyl CoA (Biotin-dependent).
• Methylmalonyl CoA → Succinyl CoA (Vitamin B12-dependent).
• Succinyl CoA → Oxaloacetate (via TCA cycle) → Glucose.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Contrast the effect of high glucagon levels on the bifunctional enzyme PFK-2/FBP-2 in favor of gluconeogenesis.
back:
• Glucagon → cAMP → Protein Kinase A.
• PFK-2 domain is phosphorylated (inactivated).
• FBP-2 domain is activated, decreasing Fructose 2,6-bisphosphate levels.
• Decreased F-2,6-BP relieves inhibition of Fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase.

category: Delineate the reactions involved in synthesis of glucose from various gluconeogenic substrates
front: Identify the primary amino acid exported from muscle during fasting to serve as a gluconeogenic precursor and how it enters the pathway.
back:
Alanine.
• Exported via the Glucose-Alanine Cycle.
• Transaminated in the liver to Pyruvate by ALT.
• Pyruvate is then carboxylated to Oxaloacetate to begin gluconeogenesis.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: The primary allosteric activator of the first step of gluconeogenesis, catalyzed by pyruvate carboxylase in the mitochondria, is [___].
back:
• Acetyl CoA.
• It signals an abundance of energy and inhibits Pyruvate Dehydrogenase.
• It diverts pyruvate away from the TCA cycle into glucose synthesis.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: A 4-month-old infant presents with hepatomegaly, severe fasting hypoglycemia, and growth retardation. Lab tests show hyperlacticacidemia and hyperuricemia. Identify the most likely enzyme deficiency.
back:
• Glucose 6-phosphatase (Von Gierke Disease).
• This enzyme is the final common step for releasing glucose from both gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Explain the role of glucagon in regulating gluconeogenesis via the PFK-2/FBPase-2 bifunctional enzyme system.
back:
• Glucagon increases cAMP, activating Protein Kinase A.
• PKA phosphorylates the bifunctional enzyme, activating the FBPase-2 domain.
• This decreases Fructose 2,6-bisphosphate levels, removing inhibition on Fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Contrast the metabolic fate of pyruvate under high versus low Acetyl CoA concentrations in the hepatocyte during the fasting state.
back:
• High Acetyl CoA: Inhibits PDH complex and activates Pyruvate Carboxylase (favors Gluconeogenesis).
• Low Acetyl CoA: Pyruvate is oxidized via PDH to enter the TCA cycle (favors ATP production).

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Identify the high-energy nucleotide triphosphate and the specific bypass enzyme required to convert oxaloacetate into phosphoenolpyruvate.
back:
• GTP (Guanosine Triphosphate).
• Enzyme: PEP Carboxykinase (PEPCK).
• This reaction involves both phosphorylation and decarboxylation.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: During gluconeogenesis, glycerol derived from adipocyte lipolysis enters the pathway as dihydroxyacetone phosphate (DHAP) after being phosphorylated by [___].
back:
• Glycerol kinase.
• This enzyme is present in the liver and kidney but absent in adipose tissue.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: A chronic alcoholic presents with hypoglycemia after a 24-hour fast. Describe the biochemical effect of the altered NADH/NAD+ ratio on gluconeogenic precursors.
back:
• Excess NADH shifts Pyruvate to Lactate.
• It shifts Oxaloacetate to Malate.
• This depletes substrates available for glucose synthesis, causing hypoglycemia.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Detail the mechanism by which oxaloacetate, produced in the mitochondria, is transferred to the cytosol for gluconeogenesis.
back:
• Oxaloacetate cannot cross the mitochondrial membrane.
• It is reduced to Malate by mitochondrial Malate Dehydrogenase.
• Malate exits via a transporter and is re-oxidized to Oxaloacetate in the cytosol.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Contrast the gluconeogenic roles and locations of the liver and the kidneys during prolonged starvation.
back:
• Liver: Main site (90%) in early fasting; releases glucose to maintain systemic levels.
• Kidneys: Becomes significant (up to 40%) in prolonged fasting; linked to ammonia production for pH buffering.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Identify the non-carbohydrate carbon source that enters the gluconeogenic pathway exclusively through the TCA cycle via succinyl CoA.
back:
• Propionate (from odd-chain fatty acids).
• It is converted to Propionyl CoA, then Methylmalonyl CoA, and finally Succinyl CoA.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: During prolonged fasting, the primary organ responsible for approximately 90% of glucose production via gluconeogenesis is the [___].
back:
• Liver
• Kidneys contribute approximately 10% initially.
• Kidney contribution increases up to 40% during long-term starvation.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: A 2-year-old with a known deficiency in Fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase presents with tremors and seizures after an 8-hour fast. Explain the metabolic failure in this patient.
back:
• Defective gluconeogenesis inhibits de novo glucose synthesis.
• Inability to bypass the phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK-1) step.
• Results in severe fasting hypoglycemia once glycogen stores are depleted.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Describe the mechanism by which Acetyl-CoA coordinates the metabolic fate of pyruvate during a fasting state.
back:
• Allosterically activates Pyruvate Carboxylase.
• Inhibits the Pyruvate Dehydrogenase (PDH) complex.
• Effectively shunts pyruvate toward gluconeogenesis instead of the TCA cycle.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Contrast the physiological stimulus and enzymatic target of Fructose 2,6-bisphosphate in glycolysis versus gluconeogenesis.
back:
• Glycolysis: Stimulated by Insulin; allosterically activates PFK-1.
• Gluconeogenesis: Inhibited by Glucagon; allosterically inhibits FBPase-1.
• Function: Prevents futile cycling by reciprocally regulating both pathways.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Identify the high-energy requirement and specific nucleotide donor used for the conversion of Oxaloacetate to Phosphoenolpyruvate.
back:
• Requires GTP (Guanosine Triphosphate).
• Catalyzed by PEP carboxykinase (PEPCK).
• Provides energy for the endergonic decarboxylation and phosphorylation step.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: The gluconeogenic enzyme [___] is unique to the endoplasmic reticulum of liver and kidney cells, allowing the release of free glucose into the systemic circulation.
back:
• Glucose 6-phosphatase
• Final common step for gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis.
• Absent in skeletal muscle, preventing it from contributing to blood glucose.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: A marathon runner experiences muscle cramping and accumulation of lactate. Explain how the Liver utilizes this metabolite to support the runner's ongoing energy needs.
back:
• Via the Cori Cycle.
• Liver oxidizes muscle-derived lactate back to pyruvate.
• Pyruvate enters gluconeogenesis to regenerate glucose, which is returned to muscle.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Explain why a "Malate Shunt" is required for gluconeogenesis starting from mitochondrial pyruvate.
back:
• Oxaloacetate (OAA) cannot cross the inner mitochondrial membrane.
• OAA is reduced to Malate by mitochondrial MDH.
• Malate exits to the cytosol and is re-oxidized to OAA to continue the pathway.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Distinguish between the gluconeogenic potential of Glycerol versus even-chain Fatty Acids in humans.
back:
• Glycerol: Enters as DHAP; provides a net source of glucose.
• Even-chain Fatty Acids: Produce Acetyl-CoA; cannot provide net glucose synthesis.
• Reason: Two carbons enter TCA as Acetyl-CoA and two are lost as CO2.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Name the essential vitamin coenzyme required by Pyruvate Carboxylase to fix carbon dioxide onto pyruvate.
back:
• Biotin (Vitamin B7).
• Covalently attached to a lysine residue of the enzyme.
• Uses ATP to activate CO2 for transfer to pyruvate.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: The conversion of pyruvate to oxaloacetate, the initial step of hepatic gluconeogenesis, is catalyzed by an enzyme requiring the prosthetic group [___].
back: ● Biotin (Vitamin B7) ● Serves as a carrier of activated CO2 ● Required for the activity of Pyruvate Carboxylase

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: A child presents with severe fasting hypoglycemia, hepatomegaly, and hyperuricemia. Laboratory tests indicate a failure to release free glucose into the blood from the endoplasmic reticulum. This points to a deficiency in [___].
back: ● Glucose 6-phosphatase ● Essential for the final step of gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis ● Diagnostic for Von Gierke Disease (Type Ia GSD)

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Explain how Acetyl-CoA acts as a critical regulatory switch for pyruvate during the fasting state in the liver.
back: ● Allosterically activates Pyruvate Carboxylase ● Inhibits Pyruvate Dehydrogenase (PDH) ● Diverts pyruvate toward glucose synthesis instead of TCA cycle oxidation

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Contrast the regulatory effect of Fructose 2,6-bisphosphate on the rate-limiting steps of Glycolysis and Gluconeogenesis.
back: ● Glycolysis: Strong allosteric activator of PFK-1 ● Gluconeogenesis: Potent allosteric inhibitor of Fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase ● Ensures pathways are not simultaneously active (Reciprocal Regulation)

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Identify the primary hormone that induces the transcription of the Phosphoenolpyruvate Carboxykinase (PEPCK) gene during starvation.
back: ● Glucagon ● Increases intracellular cAMP levels ● Promotes synthesis of PEPCK to bypass the pyruvate kinase roadblock

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: The metabolic pathway where lactate produced by anaerobic glycolysis in myocytes is transported to the liver and converted back to glucose is known as the [___] cycle.
back: ● Cori Cycle ● Prevents lactic acidosis in muscles ● Redistributes glucose for energy-dependent tissues like RBCs and brain

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
coreConcept: Metabolic Inhibition of Gluconeogenesis by Alcohol
front: A chronic alcoholic presents with profound hypoglycemia after a binge without food. Explain the biochemical basis regarding the gluconeogenic precursors lactate and malate.
back: ● Excessive NADH produced by alcohol metabolism ● Shifts equilibrium toward Lactate and Malate ● Depletes pyruvate and oxaloacetate (OAA) for glucose synthesis

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Describe the mechanism by which mitochondrial Oxaloacetate (OAA) reaches the cytosol to participate in gluconeogenesis.
back: ● OAA cannot cross mitochondrial membrane ● Reduced to Malate by mitochondrial MDH ● Malate crosses via shuttle; re-oxidized to OAA in cytosol

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Contrast the gluconeogenic potential of the amino acids Alanine and Leucine.
back: ● Alanine: Glucogenic (transaminated to pyruvate) ● Leucine: Strictly ketogenic (cannot form net glucose) ● Important for maintaining blood sugar during proteolysis

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Identify the specific organ that contributes approximately 40% of total blood glucose through gluconeogenesis during prolonged starvation.
back: ● Kidney (Renal Cortex) ● Becomes a major glucose producer after liver glycogen is depleted ● Assists in maintaining glucose for the brain

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: The [___] enzyme, which requires biotin as a co-factor, is the first regulatory step of gluconeogenesis and is obligately activated by Acetyl CoA.
back: Pyruvate Carboxylase. * Catalyzes conversion of pyruvate to oxaloacetate. * Allosterically activated by Acetyl CoA to signal high-energy states. * Provides the essential starting intermediate for hepatic glucose synthesis.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: A chronic alcoholic presents with severe fasting hypoglycemia. Metabolism of ethanol results in an elevated [___] ratio, which prevents the conversion of lactate back to pyruvate for gluconeogenesis.
back: NADH/NAD+ ratio. * Excess NADH forces the lactate dehydrogenase reaction toward lactate. * Depletes pyruvate and oxaloacetate (shifted to malate). * Effectively inhibits the gluconeogenic pathway during fasting.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Explain the role of Fructose 2,6-bisphosphate in the hormonal regulation of hepatic gluconeogenesis.
back: * It acts as a potent allosteric inhibitor of Fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase. * Glucagon decreases its concentration by activating PKA. * Lower levels relieve inhibition, allowing gluconeogenic flux toward glucose-6-phosphate.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Contrast the liver and skeletal muscle regarding the final catalytic step of gluconeogenesis and its systemic importance.
back: * Liver contains Glucose-6-Phosphatase, allowing free glucose release into blood. * Skeletal muscle lacks this enzyme; synthesized glucose remains trapped. * Only hepatic gluconeogenesis maintains blood glucose for extrahepatic tissues.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Identify the primary non-carbohydrate precursors utilized for gluconeogenesis and its critical importance during prolonged starvation.
back: * Precursors: Glucogenic amino acids, lactate, and glycerol. * Maintains glycemic levels after glycogen depletion (12-18 hours). * Essential for glucose-dependent tissues like the brain and erythrocytes.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: The metabolic pathway in which lactate produced by anaerobic glycolysis in muscles is transported to the liver and converted back to glucose is known as the [___].
back:
Cori Cycle

* Removes lactate from muscle to prevent acidosis.
* Regenerates glucose for continued muscle activity.
* Primarily active during heavy exercise.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: A marathon runner experiences muscle cramping and a drop in blood pH. The metabolic process responsible for shifting the accumulated muscle lactate to the liver to maintain blood pH and glycemia is the [___].
back:
Cori Cycle

* Prevents intracellular lactic acidosis.
* Shifts the energetic burden of gluconeogenesis to the liver.
* Recycles carbon skeletons for energy.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Explain the primary physiological role of the Glucose-Alanine cycle during periods of prolonged fasting or starvation.
back:
* Transports toxic amino groups (ammonia) from muscle to liver for urea synthesis.
* Provides pyruvate in the liver as a precursor for gluconeogenesis.
* Maintains muscle energy homeostasis and systemic nitrogen balance.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Contrast the metabolic 'waste' products carried from the muscle to the liver in the Cori cycle versus the Glucose-Alanine cycle.
back:
* Cori Cycle: Lactate (carbon skeleton only).
* Glucose-Alanine Cycle: Alanine (carbon skeleton + amino group).
* Alanine cycle handles nitrogen waste; Cori cycle handles anaerobic byproducts.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Identify the specific liver enzyme required to deaminate alanine back to pyruvate for gluconeogenesis in the Glucose-Alanine cycle.
back:
Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT / SGPT)

* Requires Pyridoxal Phosphate (B6).
* Transfers amino group to alpha-ketoglutarate, forming glutamate.
* Releases pyruvate for the gluconeogenic pathway.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: In the Glucose-Alanine cycle, the enzyme [___] is responsible for the transamination of pyruvate into alanine within skeletal muscle.
back:
Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT)

* Facilitates the safe export of nitrogen.
* Uses pyruvate as a temporary carbon carrier.
* Links protein catabolism to hepatic glucose production.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: A patient with severe liver cirrhosis presents with hyperammonemia and hypoglycemia. This clinical state suggests an impairment of the [___] cycle's ability to process nitrogen and regenerate glucose.
back:
Glucose-Alanine Cycle

* Cirrhosis prevents alanine-to-glucose conversion.
* Impairs ammonia detoxification via the urea cycle.
* Results in muscle wasting and poor glucose control.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Describe how the Cori cycle specifically aids in maintaining muscle activity during anaerobic conditions.
back:
* Prevents lactate-induced enzyme inhibition in muscles.
* Liver consumes 6 ATP to produce glucose.
* Muscle gains 2 ATP from exported glucose.
* Allows muscles to function despite oxygen debt.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Distinguish the net energetic cost of the Cori cycle in the liver versus its energetic yield in the skeletal muscle.
back:
* Liver Cost: 6 ATP (to synthesize glucose).
* Muscle Yield: 2 ATP (anaerobic glycolysis).
* Net Loss: 4 ATP per cycle for the body.
* Significance: Trades liver energy for muscle survival.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Name the two primary organs involved in the inter-organ exchange of metabolites during both the Cori and Glucose-Alanine cycles.
back:
Skeletal Muscle and Liver

* Muscle: Source of lactate and alanine.
* Liver: Site of gluconeogenesis and nitrogen processing.
* Connected via systemic circulation.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: The final step of gluconeogenesis in the liver requires the transport of glucose 6-phosphate from the cytosol into the lumen of the endoplasmic reticulum via [___].
back:
• Glucose 6-phosphate translocase
• Facilitates the bypass of the hexokinase/glucokinase reaction
• Essential for releasing free glucose into the blood

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: A 9-month-old infant presents with severe fasting hypoglycemia, hepatomegaly, and hyperlacticacidemia. A deficiency in which enzyme prevents the liver from providing free glucose from both gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis?
back:
• Glucose 6-phosphatase (Von Gierke Disease)
• Traps glucose-6-phosphate in hepatocytes
• Results in massive glycogen accumulation and metabolic acidosis

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Explain the role of Glucagon in modulating the Fructose 1,6-bisphosphate/Fructose 6-phosphate cycle during fasting.
back:
• Glucagon increases cAMP/PKA
• PKA phosphorylates PFK-2/FBPase-2, activating the phosphatase domain
• Fructose 2,6-bisphosphate levels fall
• This removes inhibition from FBPase-1, stimulating gluconeogenesis

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Contrast the significance of gluconeogenesis in the liver versus the kidneys during prolonged starvation (e.g., several weeks).
back:
• Liver: Site of 90% production during overnight fast; decreases relative contribution later
• Kidneys: Contribution increases to ~40% during prolonged fast
• Kidney gluconeogenesis helps compensate for ketoacidosis via glutamine-derived ammonia

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Provide the biochemical reason why even-chain fatty acids cannot contribute to the net synthesis of glucose in humans.
back:
• Metabolism yields only Acetyl-CoA
• Pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) reaction is irreversible
• Two carbons enter TCA cycle as Acetyl-CoA and two leave as CO2
• No net increase in oxaloacetate exists

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: During vigorous exercise, the liver maintains blood glucose by converting lactate into glucose via the [___].
back:
• Cori Cycle
• Prevents lactic acidosis in muscle
• Requires 6 ATP equivalents per glucose molecule synthesized

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: A chronic alcoholic presents with severe hypoglycemia. The high NADH:NAD+ ratio from ethanol metabolism inhibits gluconeogenesis primarily by shifting the [___] equilibrium towards malate.
back:
• Oxaloacetate (OAA)
• High NADH reduces OAA to malate, depleting the precursor
• Also shifts pyruvate toward lactate
• Prevents OAA from entering the PEPCK bypass

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Describe the mechanism by which Phosphoenolpyruvate Carboxykinase (PEPCK) bypasses the irreversible pyruvate kinase reaction.
back:
• Converts oxaloacetate (OAA) to phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP)
• Requires GTP as the phosphate donor
• Coupled with decarboxylation to drive the endergonic synthesis
• Transcription is induced by glucagon/cortisol

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Contrast the effects of Fructose 2,6-bisphosphate on its two target enzymes in the liver.
back:
• PFK-1: Potent allosteric activator; stimulates glycolysis
• FBPase-1: Potent allosteric inhibitor; blocks gluconeogenesis
• Result: Prevents futile cycling at the triose-phosphate level

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Name the specific non-carbohydrate precursor derived from adipose tissue that enters gluconeogenesis via dihydroxyacetone phosphate (DHAP).
back:
• Glycerol
• Phosphorylated to Glycerol-3-P by hepatic Glycerol kinase
• Oxidized to DHAP by Glycerol-3-P dehydrogenase
• Only gluconeogenic substrate derived from lipids

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: The metabolic pathway where muscle-derived lactate is transported to the liver via the blood for conversion back into glucose is known as the [___] cycle.
back:
• Cori Cycle.
• Prevents lactic acidosis during anaerobic exercise.
• Recycles carbon for hepatic gluconeogenesis.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: A sprinter experiences muscle cramping and a drop in blood pH after a 100m dash. The metabolic loop that helps resolve this by recycling the accumulated metabolite in the liver is the [___].
back:
• Cori Cycle.
• Clears muscle lactate.
• Converts lactate to pyruvate, then to glucose via gluconeogenesis.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Explain how the glucose-alanine cycle handles toxic nitrogen produced during skeletal muscle protein catabolism.
back:
• Muscle nitrogen is transferred to pyruvate to form alanine.
• Alanine carries nitrogen safely to the liver.
• Liver releases nitrogen for urea synthesis and recycles carbon.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
coreConcept: Energetic Cost of the Cori Cycle
front: Contrast the ATP balance of the Cori cycle between the skeletal muscle and the liver components.
back:
• Muscle: Produces 2 ATP (anaerobic glycolysis).
• Liver: Consumes 6 ATP (gluconeogenesis).
• Net Result: Energy cost of 4 ATP per cycle turn.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
coreConcept: ALT and PLP in Amino Acid Transport
front: Identify the primary transaminase enzyme and its required vitamin B6-derived cofactor involved in the glucose-alanine cycle.
back:
• Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT).
• Pyridoxal Phosphate (PLP/B6).
• Facilitates the transamination between pyruvate and alanine.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: In the glucose-alanine cycle, the specific amino acid that serves as a non-toxic carrier of ammonia from skeletal muscle to the liver is [___].
back:
• Alanine.
• Prevents systemic ammonia toxicity during protein breakdown.
• Provides pyruvate for hepatic gluconeogenesis.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: During prolonged starvation, skeletal muscle breaks down protein for fuel. Describe the significance of the alanine cycle in blood glucose maintenance in this state.
back:
• Muscle provides alanine as a gluconeogenic substrate.
• Liver converts alanine to glucose for brain/RBC use.
• Crucial for glucose homeostasis when glycogen is depleted.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Describe why the Cori cycle is physiologically essential for erythrocytes (RBCs) compared to other cells.
back:
• RBCs lack mitochondria and rely solely on anaerobic glycolysis.
• Cori cycle clears their constant lactate output.
• Maintains RBC ATP levels and prevents systemic pH drop.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Distinguish between the Cori cycle and the glucose-alanine cycle regarding their primary "cargo" transported from muscle to liver.
back:
• Cori Cycle: Transports Lactate (Carbon only).
• Glucose-Alanine Cycle: Transports Alanine (Carbon plus amino nitrogen).

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Name the two primary organs involved in the exchange of metabolites during both the Cori and glucose-alanine cycles.
back:
• Skeletal Muscle (source tissue).
• Liver (recycling/processing center).
• Interconnected via the blood circulation.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: The primary gluconeogenic enzyme that bypasses the irreversible phosphofructokinase-1 step of glycolysis is [___].
back:
- Fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase.
- Inhibited by AMP and Fructose 2,6-bisphosphate.
- Activated by high ATP levels.
- Key regulatory site of the pathway.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: A chronic alcoholic presents with fasting hypoglycemia. The excessive NADH generated by ethanol metabolism shifts the malate dehydrogenase equilibrium toward [___], depleting oxaloacetate for gluconeogenesis.
back:
- Malate.
- High NADH/NAD+ ratio drives OAA reduction to Malate.
- Depletes OAA, a vital gluconeogenic precursor.
- Result: Impaired glucose synthesis and clinical hypoglycemia.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Explain the 'protein-sparing effect' of dietary carbohydrates during prolonged fasting.
back:
- Adequate carbohydrate intake prevents gluconeogenesis.
- Stops the mobilization of glucogenic amino acids.
- Preserves skeletal muscle protein from degradation.
- Ensures glucose is supplied from dietary sources rather than tissue breakdown.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Contrast the physiological role of the liver versus skeletal muscle regarding the expression of the enzyme Glucose 6-phosphatase.
back:
- Liver: Contains enzyme; releases free glucose into systemic circulation.
- Skeletal Muscle: Lacks enzyme; Glucose 6-P is trapped for local glycolysis.
- Result: Muscle cannot contribute to blood glucose maintenance.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Identify the primary therapeutic mechanism of Metformin in managing Type 2 Diabetes regarding hepatic metabolism.
back:
- Inhibition of hepatic gluconeogenesis.
- Reduces glucose output from the liver.
- Lowers fasting blood glucose levels.
- Improves insulin sensitivity in peripheral tissues.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: An infant presenting with severe fasting hypoglycemia, hepatomegaly, and 'doll-like' facies is diagnosed with Von Gierke disease, caused by a deficiency in [___].
back:
- Glucose 6-phosphatase.
- Affects both gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis.
- Leads to intracellular trapping of Glucose 6-P.
- Results in severe hypoglycemia and lactic acidosis.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: A marathon runner relies on the 'Cori Cycle' to maintain blood glucose. Describe the movement of substrates between the muscle and liver in this cycle.
back:
- Muscle: Converts glucose to Lactate during exercise.
- Blood: Transports Lactate to the liver.
- Liver: Converts Lactate back to Glucose via gluconeogenesis.
- Blood: Returns Glucose to muscle/RBCs.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Explain the transcriptional regulation of the PEP-carboxykinase (PEPCK) gene in response to the Glucagon-to-Insulin ratio.
back:
- Glucagon: Increases PEPCK gene transcription via cAMP pathway.
- Insulin: Represses PEPCK gene expression.
- Fasting state: High Glucagon induces PEPCK synthesis to increase glucose production.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Contrast the effect of Glucagon on hepatic Pyruvate Kinase (PK) with its effect on the skeletal muscle isozyme.
back:
- Liver: Inactivates PK via cAMP-dependent phosphorylation.
- Skeletal Muscle: PK is not affected by Glucagon.
- Significance: Liver PK inhibition prevents a 'futile cycle' during gluconeogenesis.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
coreConcept: Importance of Gluconeogenesis in Avascular Tissues
front: State the physiological importance of gluconeogenesis for the maintenance of the lens and cornea of the eye.
back:
- These tissues are poorly vascularized and lack mitochondria.
- They depend exclusively on anaerobic glycolysis.
- Gluconeogenesis ensures a continuous glucose supply during fasting to prevent metabolic failure.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: During anaerobic muscle contraction, the metabolic intermediate [___] is exported to the liver to be converted into glucose via the Cori cycle.
back:
• Lactate
• Produced by muscle LDH during glycolysis
• Recycled into glucose by liver gluconeogenesis
• Prevents lactic acid accumulation

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: A 22-year-old athlete performing a high-intensity sprint relies on a metabolic loop to maintain muscle NAD+ levels and blood glucose without local accumulation of protons. Identify this cycle's primary significance in this physiological context.
back:
• Cori Cycle
• Regenerates NAD+ for anaerobic glycolysis
• Shifts the metabolic burden of gluconeogenesis to the liver
• Prevents systemic metabolic acidosis

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Explain the role of the glucose-alanine cycle in the safe transport of nitrogen from peripheral tissues during periods of muscle proteolysis.
back:
• Pyruvate is transaminated to Alanine
• Alanine carries toxic ammonia to the liver
• Liver ALT releases the nitrogen for the Urea Cycle
• Pyruvate is then used for gluconeogenesis

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Contrast the Cori cycle and the glucose-alanine cycle regarding the specific 'muscle byproduct' each cycle primarily aims to clear from the myocytes.
back:
• Cori Cycle clears Lactate (managing pH)
• Glucose-Alanine clears Ammonia (managing nitrogen toxicity)
• Both return glucose to the muscle
• Both depend on hepatic gluconeogenesis

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: State the net ATP cost to the liver for every molecule of glucose regenerated via the Cori cycle during active inter-organ metabolic flux.
back:
• 4 ATP (Net cost)
• 6 ATP consumed in liver gluconeogenesis
• 2 ATP produced in muscle glycolysis
• Ensures muscle work can continue anaerobically

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: In the glucose-alanine cycle, the conversion of pyruvate to alanine in skeletal muscle is catalyzed by the enzyme [___].
back:
• Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT)
• Requires Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxal Phosphate)
• Essential for nitrogen transfer to liver
• Pairs glutamate/alpha-ketoglutarate with pyruvate/alanine

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: A patient with severe liver cirrhosis presents with hyperammonemia. Despite normal muscle mass, the inability to process nitrogen from muscle breakdown into glucose suggests a failure in which specificinter-organ cycle?
back:
• Glucose-Alanine Cycle
• Liver failure stops alanine-to-urea conversion
• Impairs nitrogen clearance and gluconeogenesis
• Leads to accumulation of toxic metabolites in blood

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Describe how the glucose-alanine cycle acts as a protein-sparing mechanism during prolonged fasting.
back:
• Transports amino groups for urea excretion
• Recycles carbon skeletons for glucose production
• Minimizes the need for continuous whole-protein breakdown
• Supplies essential glucose to the brain/RBCs

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Distinguish between the substrates returned to the muscle in both the Cori and Glucose-Alanine cycles.
back:
• Substrate: Glucose (identical in both)
• Cori sends Lactate out of muscle
• Alanine sends Alanine out of muscle
• Both rely on blood transport and liver enzymes

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Name the two primary intracellular locations where the enzymes for gluconeogenesis are located when completing the Cori cycle in the liver.
back:
• Mitochondria (Pyruvate to Oxaloacetate)
• Cytosol (Oxaloacetate to Glucose)
• Required to bridge lactate to glucose
• Highly energy-intensive process

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: In the Cori cycle, the specific metabolite produced by anaerobic glycolysis in skeletal muscle that is subsequently transported to the liver for gluconeogenesis is [___].
back:
• Lactate.
• Produced during vigorous exercise.
• Reconverted to glucose in the liver via gluconeogenesis.
• Prevents excessive lactic acid accumulation in muscle.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: A marathon runner experiences muscle fatigue and localized acidosis. The biochemical pathway responsible for recycling his muscle-derived lactate into hepatic glucose to maintain performance is the [___].
back:
• Cori Cycle (Lactic acid cycle).
• Connects muscle glycolysis to liver gluconeogenesis.
• Essential for sustained glucose supply during anaerobic conditions.
• Costs 6 ATP in liver; produces 2 ATP in muscle.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Explain the primary physiological purpose of the Glucose-Alanine cycle during periods of prolonged fasting.
back:
• Transports amino groups from muscle to liver.
• Provides carbon skeletons for gluconeogenesis.
• Assists in non-toxic ammonia detoxification via the Urea Cycle.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Contrast the metabolic fate of the nitrogen group in the Glucose-Alanine cycle versus the Cori cycle.
back:
• Glucose-Alanine cycle: Nitrogen is removed and converted to urea in the liver.
• Cori cycle: No nitrogen transport occurs; only carbon (as lactate) is recycled.
• Alanine cycle involves protein catabolism.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Identify the hepatic enzyme required for the initial step of the Glucose-Alanine cycle to regenerate pyruvate from alanine.
back:
• Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT/SGPT).
• Requires Pyridoxal Phosphate (Vitamin B6) as a cofactor.
• Transfers amino group from alanine to alpha-ketoglutarate to form glutamate.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: The Cori cycle occurs primarily under anaerobic conditions, whereas the Glucose-Alanine cycle is more characteristically associated with the metabolic state of [___].
back:
• Prolonged fasting or starvation.
• Linked to skeletal muscle protein breakdown.
• Maintains blood glucose when carbohydrate stores are depleted.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: A patient with severe liver cirrhosis exhibits hypoglycemia and hyperammonemia. Which specific component of the inter-organ cycle between muscle and liver is compromised in this scenario?
back:
• Hepatic gluconeogenesis and the Urea cycle.
• Liver cannot process alanine back into glucose.
• Failure to detoxify transported nitrogen leads to ammonia buildup.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Detail the net energetic cost (in ATP units) incurred by the liver during one full turn of the Cori cycle.
back:
• 6 ATP consumed.
• Required to drive gluconeogenesis from two lactate molecules.
• Net organismal loss is 4 ATP (6 spent in liver minus 2 gained in muscle).

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Distinguish between the skeletal muscle substrates produced for hepatic transport in the Cori cycle versus the Glucose-Alanine cycle.
back:
• Cori Cycle: Substrate is Lactate (from pyruvate reduction).
• Glucose-Alanine Cycle: Substrate is Alanine (from pyruvate transamination).
• Both regenerate glucose to be sent back to muscle.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: State the primary advantage of using alanine instead of free ammonia as a nitrogen transport molecule from muscle to liver.
back:
• Alanine is non-toxic to the brain and blood.
• Free ammonia is highly neurotoxic.
• Alanine carries both nitrogen (for urea) and carbon (for glucose) simultaneously.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: The most potent allosteric inhibitor of the rate-limiting enzyme in gluconeogenesis, fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase, is [___].
back: - Fructose 2,6-bisphosphate (F2,6BP). - Its concentration decreases in response to high glucagon levels. - This reduction in F2,6BP relieves inhibition on FBP-1, thereby accelerating gluconeogenesis.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: A 4-month-old infant presents with severe fasting hypoglycemia, hepatomegaly, and hyperlacticacidemia. A liver biopsy reveals excessive glycogen stores with a normal structure. Identify the enzyme deficiency and its primary effect on gluconeogenesis.
back: - Glucose 6-phosphatase deficiency (Von Gierke Disease). - It prevents the final step of gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis. - Free glucose cannot be released from the liver into the systemic circulation.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Describe the biochemical pathway by which glycerol derived from adipose triacylglycerols is converted into a gluconeogenic intermediate.
back: - Glycerol is phosphorylated to glycerol phosphate by glycerol kinase in the liver. - It is then oxidized to dihydroxyacetone phosphate (DHAP) by glycerol phosphate dehydrogenase. - DHAP enters the gluconeogenic pathway directly.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Contrast the metabolic fates of phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) in the liver during the well-fed state versus the fasting state under the influence of glucagon.
back: - Well-fed state: PEP is converted to pyruvate by active Pyruvate Kinase (glycolysis). - Fasting state: Pyruvate Kinase is inactivated by cAMP-dependent phosphorylation. - Result: PEP is diverted toward glucose synthesis (gluconeogenesis).

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Explain why skeletal muscle is unable to provide free glucose to the blood during a fast even though it possesses significant glycogen stores.
back: - Muscle lacks the enzyme glucose 6-phosphatase. - It cannot dephosphorylate glucose 6-phosphate into free glucose. - Glucose 6-phosphate produced by muscle is instead used locally to fuel anaerobic glycolysis.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Gluconeogenesis becomes the essential source of blood glucose after hepatic glycogen stores are significantly depleted, typically after [___] hours of fasting.
back: - 10 to 18 hours. - It serves as a continuous glucose supply for glucose-dependent tissues like the brain and RBCs. - During prolonged starvation, renal gluconeogenesis contributes up to 40% of total production.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: A patient with a glucagon-secreting tumor (glucagonoma) exhibits persistent hyperglycemia. How does chronic glucagon elevation influence the gene expression of Phosphoenolpyruvate Carboxykinase (PEPCK)?
back: - Glucagon increases the transcription of the PEPCK gene. - Elevated mRNA levels lead to increased synthesis of the PEPCK enzyme. - This enhances the conversion of oxaloacetate into phosphoenolpyruvate, promoting glucose synthesis.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Detail the energetic coupling mechanism by which fatty acid oxidation in the liver supports the high metabolic cost of gluconeogenesis.
back: - Beta-oxidation provides the ATP required for the synthetic reactions. - Oxidation increases the mitochondrial NADH/NAD ratio, favoring the gluconeogenic direction. - Acetyl CoA accumulation allosterically activates pyruvate carboxylase.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Differentiate between the subcellular location of the first step of gluconeogenesis (pyruvate to oxaloacetate) and the final step (glucose 6-phosphate to glucose).
back: - First Step: Occurs in the Mitochondria (pyruvate carboxylase). - Final Step: Occurs in the Endoplasmic Reticulum (glucose 6-phosphatase). - Intermediate Steps: Occurs primarily in the Cytosol.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Identify the high-energy nucleotide triphosphate required specifically by the enzyme PEP-carboxykinase to drive the conversion of oxaloacetate to phosphoenolpyruvate.
back: - Guanosine triphosphate (GTP). - This reaction involves both phosphorylation and decarboxylation. - The overall stoichiometry of gluconeogenesis requires 6 high-energy phosphate bonds per glucose molecule produced.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: The metabolic pathway responsible for preventing systemic lactic acidosis by recycling muscle-derived lactate into hepatic glucose is the [___].
back:
• Cori Cycle (Lactic Acid Cycle)
• Converts lactate to glucose in the liver.
• Sustains anaerobic energy for muscle/RBCs.
• Relieves the body of excess protons.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: A marathon runner experiences intense muscle catabolism. Biochemical analysis reveals high levels of amino groups being transported to the liver via a specific carbon carrier to maintain blood glucose. Identify this cycle.
back:
• Glucose-Alanine Cycle (Cahill Cycle)
• Transports nitrogen from muscle to liver.
• Uses alanine as the primary carrier.
• Provides a glucose source during prolonged exercise.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Explain the role of the liver in supporting skeletal muscle during the anaerobic phase of the Cori cycle.
back:
• Uptake: Liver absorbs lactate from the bloodstream.
• Conversion: Lactate is oxidized to pyruvate via LDH.
• Gluconeogenesis: Pyruvate is converted to glucose.
• Recycling: Glucose is released back to muscle.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Contrast the primary metabolic purposes of the Cori cycle versus the Glucose-Alanine cycle regarding nitrogen handling.
back:
• Cori Cycle: Primarily for carbon recycling and anaerobic energy (no nitrogen involvement).
• Glucose-Alanine: Dual role of carbon recycling and safe transport of toxic ammonia (nitrogen) to the liver.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Identify the hepatic metabolic byproduct synthesized as a direct consequence of the nitrogen delivered by the Glucose-Alanine cycle.
back:
• Urea
• Alanine is deaminated in the liver.
• Released ammonia enters the Urea Cycle.
• Resulting pyruvate enters gluconeogenesis.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: While the liver serves as the central hub for glucose production, the peripheral tissue that initiates the Glucose-Alanine cycle is [___].
back:
• Skeletal muscle
• Breakdown of muscle protein provides amino groups.
• Glycolysis provides the pyruvate backbone.
• Essential for nitrogen balance during fasting.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: A patient with advanced liver cirrhosis develops hypoglycemia and persistent lactic acidosis after minor exertion. Explain the failure of inter-organ cycling in this patient.
back:
• Impaired hepatic gluconeogenesis prevents the conversion of lactate to glucose.
• Disruption of the Cori Cycle arm.
• Leads to accumulation of lactate and glucose deficiency.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Describe the specific transamination reaction in skeletal muscle required to synthesize alanine for the Glucose-Alanine cycle.
back:
• Enzyme: Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT).
• Reactants: Pyruvate accepts an amino group from Glutamate.
• Products: Alanine and Alpha-ketoglutarate.
• Purpose: Packages nitrogen into a non-toxic carrier.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Distinguish the net ATP balance of the Cori cycle between the muscle and the liver components.
back:
• Muscle: Net gain of 2 ATP (anaerobic glycolysis).
• Liver: Net loss of 6 ATP (gluconeogenesis).
• Overall System: Net cost of 4 ATP to the body.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Name the common three-carbon intermediate into which both lactate and alanine must be converted before entering hepatic gluconeogenesis.
back:
• Pyruvate
• Lactate is oxidized to pyruvate (LDH).
• Alanine is transaminated to pyruvate (ALT).
• Both then enter the gluconeogenic pathway.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: During the Cori cycle, the metabolite [___] is transported from skeletal muscle to the liver to be converted back into glucose via gluconeogenesis.
back:
• Lactate
• Produced during anaerobic glycolysis in muscle
• Converted to pyruvate by hepatic LDH
• Critical for recycling NAD+ and preventing systemic lactic acidosis

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: During intense exercise, a sprinter's skeletal muscle produces alanine to handle ammonia produced by amino acid catabolism. The specific muscle enzyme that catalyzes the transfer of an amino group to pyruvate to form this alanine is [___].
back:
• Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT)
• Uses pyruvate as the amino group acceptor
• Creates alanine as a non-toxic nitrogen carrier
• Transfers nitrogen from muscle to liver urea cycle

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Explain the biochemical significance of the glucose-alanine cycle regarding nitrogen homeostasis during periods of high muscle protein turnover.
back:
• Facilitates safe transport of muscle ammonia to liver
• Provides pyruvate for hepatic gluconeogenesis
• Links muscle protein catabolism to liver urea synthesis
• Prevents ammonia toxicity in peripheral tissues

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
coreConcept: Differential Contrast: Cori vs. Alanine Cycle
front: Contrast the Cori cycle and the glucose-alanine cycle based on the type of byproduct recycled and the specific physiological need addressed.
back:
• Cori: Recycles lactate; addresses anaerobic ATP needs and pH balance
• Alanine: Recycles alanine; addresses nitrogen excretion and protein turnover
• Both: Utilize hepatic gluconeogenesis to maintain blood glucose
• Major Difference: Alanine cycle delivers nitrogen; Cori does not

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Identify the primary enzymatic deficiency in skeletal muscle that necessitates the involvement of the liver in both the Cori and glucose-alanine cycles.
back:
• Absence of Glucose 6-phosphatase
• Prevents muscle from releasing free glucose into blood
• Requires liver to perform the final step of gluconeogenesis
• Ensures glucose availability for active muscle fibers

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: The metabolic pathway where lactate produced by anaerobic glycolysis in skeletal muscle is transported to the liver to be converted back into glucose is known as the [___] cycle.
back: * Cori Cycle. * Recycles lactate to prevent lactic acidosis. * Sustains blood glucose during intense exercise.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: A 25-year-old athlete experiences muscle fatigue and a drop in tissue pH during a sprint. The inter-organ biochemical cycle responsible for removing the accumulating metabolite to prevent further acidosis is the [___].
back: * Cori Cycle (Lactic acid cycle). * Shifts metabolic burden from muscle to liver. * Allows continued anaerobic energy production.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Explain the role of the glucose-alanine cycle in nitrogen metabolism during periods of prolonged fasting.
back: * Muscle protein breaks down into amino acids. * Amino groups are transferred to pyruvate to form Alanine. * Alanine safely transports nitrogen to the liver for urea synthesis.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Contrast the energetic cost of the Cori cycle in the liver with the net ATP yield in the muscle during anaerobic glycolysis.
back: * Muscle Yield: 2 ATP per glucose. * Liver Cost: 6 ATP (for gluconeogenesis). * Net Balance: Loss of 4 high-energy phosphates per cycle.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: State the primary role of the glucose-alanine cycle regarding skeletal muscle transamination.
back: * Provides a safe, non-toxic transport of ammonia. * Facilitates glucose-nitrogen exchange between tissues. * Recycles carbon skeletons for gluconeogenesis.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: In the glucose-alanine cycle, the enzyme responsible for the transamination of pyruvate into alanine within skeletal muscle is [___].
back: * Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT). * Requires Pyridoxal Phosphate (Vitamin B6). * Essential for converting amino groups into transportable alanine.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: After a 48-hour fast, a patient's muscle proteins are degraded. Identify the specific cycle that transports the resulting carbon skeletons and amino groups to the liver for both urea synthesis and glucose production.
back: * Glucose-Alanine Cycle. * Supports brain metabolism via gluconeogenesis. * Disposes of nitrogenous waste via the liver.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Describe the biochemical fate of alanine once it reaches the liver during the Cahill cycle.
back: * Deaminated back to Pyruvate. * Amino group enters the Urea Cycle for excretion. * Pyruvate enters Gluconeogenesis to regenerate blood glucose.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Distinguish between the Cori cycle and the Glucose-Alanine cycle based on the specific carrier molecule used for carbon transport.
back: * Cori Cycle: Uses Lactate (lacks nitrogen). * Glucose-Alanine Cycle: Uses Alanine (carries nitrogen). * Both cycles recycle 3-carbon units for gluconeogenesis.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Name the two primary organs involved in the inter-organ exchange of metabolites during the Cori and Glucose-Alanine cycles.
back: * Skeletal Muscle (Producer). * Liver (Recycler/Processor). * Connected through blood circulation.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Long-term hormonal regulation of gluconeogenesis is achieved via the induction of the gene for [___], the rate-limiting enzyme that converts oxaloacetate to phosphoenolpyruvate.
back: * Phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase (PEPCK). * Increases total enzyme concentration in the liver. * Acts at the level of gene transcription. * Promoted by Glucagon and Cortisol during fasting.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: A chronic alcoholic presents with profound fasting hypoglycemia. The depletion of gluconeogenic substrates occurs because the high NADH:NAD+ ratio prevents the conversion of [___] to Dihydroxyacetone phosphate (DHAP).
back: * Glycerol 3-phosphate. * High NADH:NAD+ ratio shifts equilibrium toward Glycerol 3-P. * Depletes the pool of DHAP available for glucose synthesis. * Primary cause of alcoholic hypoglycemia.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Explain the physiological importance of gluconeogenesis in maintaining metabolic homeostasis during prolonged starvation.
back: * Prevents hypoglycemia after liver glycogen depletion (>18 hours). * Provides essential fuel for brain and erythrocytes. * Clears lactic acid from peripheral tissues (Cori Cycle). * Maintains carbon skeletons for biosynthetic intermediates.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Contrast the regulatory effects of Fructose 2,6-bisphosphate on Phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK-1) versus Fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase (FBPase-1).
back: * Activates PFK-1: Potently stimulates glycolysis by increasing F6P affinity. * Inhibits FBPase-1: Potently suppresses gluconeogenesis. * Level controlled by bifunctional enzyme (PFK-2/FBPase-2) under insulin/glucagon control.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Identify the three primary non-carbohydrate carbon sources utilized by the liver for glucose synthesis during the early stages of a fast.
back: * Glucogenic amino acids (primarily Alanine from muscle). * Lactate (from anaerobic glycolysis in RBCs/muscle). * Glycerol (from triacylglycerol breakdown in adipose). * Essential for maintaining glucose during glycogenolysis transition.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: The final step of gluconeogenesis, localized to the luminal surface of the endoplasmic reticulum to allow glucose release into blood, is catalyzed by the enzyme [___].
back: * Glucose 6-phosphatase. * Localized specifically in the ER lumen. * Absent in skeletal muscle (prevents glucose release). * Essential for systemic glucose delivery.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: A neonate with hepatomegaly and severe fasting hypoglycemia is diagnosed with Von Gierke Disease. Explain the pathophysiology of the hypoglycemia in this condition.
back: * Glucose 6-phosphatase deficiency. * Impairs final common step of gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis. * G6P cannot be dephosphorylated to free glucose. * Massive intracellular accumulation drives lipid and lactate synthesis.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Detail the molecular mechanism by which Glucagon prevents a futile cycle between Phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) and Pyruvate in the liver during starvation.
back: * Increases cAMP, activating Protein Kinase A (PKA). * PKA phosphorylates and inactivates Pyruvate Kinase (L-isozyme). * Inhibits conversion of PEP back to Pyruvate. * Forces PEP to move upward toward glucose synthesis.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Distinguish between hepatic and renal gluconeogenesis regarding their contributions to systemic glucose levels during prolonged starvation.
back: * Liver: Primary site (90%) for glucose production in early fasting. * Kidney: Responsible for up to 40% during prolonged starvation. * Kidney utilizes glutamine, helping maintain acid-base balance.

category: Elaborate the regulation and importance of gluconeogenesis
front: Describe the primary role of Glucocorticoids (Cortisol) in maintaining substrate availability for the gluconeogenic pathway.
back: * Stimulate proteolysis: Break down muscle protein into amino acids. * Provide glucogenic precursors (Alanine, Glutamine) to liver. * Upregulate PEPCK synthesis at the genetic level. * Act synergistically with Glucagon.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: The metabolic pathway responsible for shuttling lactate produced by anaerobic glycolysis in skeletal muscle to the liver for gluconeogenesis is the [___].
back:
• Cori Cycle (Lactic Acid Cycle).
• It prevents lactic acidosis in muscle.
• It regenerates glucose to be used again by peripheral tissues.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: A 22-year-old male athlete performs an intensive sprint. His muscles produce significant lactate. Identify the specific enzymatic reaction in the liver that initiates the recycling of this lactate into glucose.
back:
• Lactate Dehydrogenase (LDH) reaction.
• LDH converts lactate back into pyruvate.
• Pyruvate then enters the gluconeogenesis pathway.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Explain the role of the Glucose-Alanine cycle in managing skeletal muscle nitrogen during periods of protein catabolism.
back:
• Pyruvate is transaminated to Alanine.
• Alanine carries amino groups from muscle to the liver.
• This facilitates safe nitrogen disposal via the Urea Cycle.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Contrast the Cori cycle and the Glucose-Alanine cycle regarding their specific impact on systemic nitrogen homeostasis.
back:
• Cori Cycle: No nitrogen involvement; only carbon (lactate) transport.
• Glucose-Alanine Cycle: Essential for nitrogen transport; alanine carries amino groups to the liver for urea synthesis.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Identify the net ATP cost to the liver for every two molecules of lactate converted back into one molecule of glucose via the Cori cycle.
back:
• 6 ATP molecules.
• The cycle is energy-expensive for the liver.
• This allows muscles to continue functioning under anaerobic conditions.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: In the glucose-alanine cycle, the enzyme [___] is required to transfer an amino group from glutamate to pyruvate to form alanine in muscle tissue.
back:
• Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT).
• It requires Pyridoxal Phosphate (Vitamin B6).
• It is also known as Glutamate-Pyruvate Transaminase (GPT).

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: A patient with severe liver cirrhosis exhibits fasting hypoglycemia. How does this pathology disrupt the metabolic significance of the Cahill (Glucose-Alanine) cycle?
back:
• Impairs hepatic gluconeogenesis.
• The liver cannot convert muscle-derived alanine back into glucose.
• Leads to failure in blood glucose maintenance and potential hyperammonemia.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
front: Describe why skeletal muscle must utilize the Cori or Alanine cycles instead of simply releasing free glucose from glycogen into the blood.
back:
• Muscle lacks Glucose-6-Phosphatase.
• Glucose-6-Phosphate cannot cross cell membranes.
• Muscle must export lactate or alanine for the liver to produce free glucose.

category: Explain the significance of Cori cycle and glucosealanine cycle
